fields.title: Provincial Health Extender
fields.body:
Overview of position

- In 2021 an L3 emergency was announced in Afghanistan following change in power in the country. our client Health programme worked with partners to provide essential health services for children and women in need across the country. Services are provided through health facilities and mobile teams for remote, hard-to-reach and in-need areas. Monitoring and technical support are key functions to verify programme implementation and improve the quality of service, including MNCAH, EPI, and especially health in emergency activities in all provinces of the country, as well as at the regional and national levels.
- In addition, in September 2021, the world bank suspended the Sehatmandi project in Afghanistan, this threatens to collapse the health system in the country, our client and WHO have worked to sustain the services through CERF fund until a new mechanism is created. A monitoring framework of this modality is being created including monitoring field visits to health facilities receiving support through our client.
- Also, in 2021, vaccination against COVID 19 started in the country, adding more burden to the already overwhelmed health system, the introduction of new vaccine targeting different population groups, required another additional monitoring framework and tools to track the progress and ensue quality and equity.
- Objective: Extenders are expected to carry out a range of duties, as outlined below, to support monitoring functions, demand generation, accountability to affected population mechanisms, technical facilitation and programme implementation.
- Those duties, which are described in detail below, do not include neither programmatic nor financial authority. Extenders are identified among Afghani citizens with specific expertise and a thorough knowledge of the territory in which they operate, based on their residency and/or work experience.
- Due to the current emergency situation in the county and the growing needs in all areas (total health PiN in 2022 is 18.4 M) which led to a quick increase of emergency activities supported by our client, and due to the difficult geographical nature of Afghanistan and the lack of transportation infrastructure and the remoteness of many communities, which make access and monitoring a challenge in many areas. The need of our client extenders network to complement our client efforts in such areas (difficult to access by staff) is critical to achieve the programme goals. Extenders are engaged through a third-party Service Provider that is directly responsible for the administrative and security related aspects of the Extenders deployment, while our client is responsible for financial support, technical guidance and supervision.
- Accordingly, the Extenders will be contracted by a Service Provider and will be considered a staff of the contracting company for all purposes and in all circumstances. The Extenders will not be considered a our client staff member or consultant. As such, our client will not be directly or indirectly responsible for the Extenders while implementing this Terms of Reference (TOR).
- Based on the approved RWP, our client is supporting MNCAH and EPI services in the country and working to improve coordination, develop policies, strategies, and guidelines, support implementation and monitoring of activities. extenders are tasked to facilitate and support our client programme activities implementation and monitoring tasks that cannot be done by our client staff due to accessibility, security, and scale. Which make extenders modality the most reliable and efficient way to support those tasks.
- Extender will be based at their area of responsibility, and usually selected from communities in same area for easy mobility and to reduce security risks, and transportation time and cost. These extenders are not given task that is supposed to be done normally by our client staff.

Role objectives

TASK TO BE PERFORMED

- Conduct regular situation monitoring in specific areas based on requests by the programme or Zonal Office, to assess the overall humanitarian situation and document the needs of affected populations, in particular women and children health needs.
- Provide technical services to our client projects primarily in hard-to-reach areas, through ensuring regular and systematic technical advice, quality assurance and technical guidance to implementing partners and counterparts, for the efficient implementation of our client programmes and effective achievement of results for the benefit of Afghani children and women.
- Identify capacity and technical gaps of implementing partners and counterparts and provide technical support to ensure capacity building and on job training as needed.
- Support the implementation of Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNT) supported by our client through technical support and capacity building, and monitor the service implementation and quality. and work with partners at the provincial level to improve MHNT programme results.
- Monitor the work of health facilities supported through our client CERF and other funds using the common checklists and tools.
- Support EPI programme routine immunization activities including -but not limited to- service delivery, cold chain system, vaccine and non-vaccine supplies, information system.
- Support emergency preparedness and response activities implementation and monitoring.
- Report any suspected PSEA case directly to the responsible our client focal point and inform the programme specialist.
- Report any suspected fraud case to the Zonal programme specialist or relevant our client staff.
- Coordinate the monthly working\\monitoring plan with the regional extender, and share the progress and visits repots on timely manner.
- Participating in PHCC, Staff meeting with SP, EPI sub comettee and relvent meetings.

Conduct regular visits to monitor Health programme activities supported by our client, and facilitate our client staff programmatic visits, with a focus on:

- Assessing programme implementation by Implementing Partners through PCAs (Programme Cooperation Agreements) and SSFAs (Small-Scale Funding Agreements) as well as programme implementation by partners and agencies according to the our client Afghanistan Country Office Work Plans.
- Checking EPI supplies chain systems and equipment in place and their functionality status, including following SOPs in vaccine storage and utilization.
- Supporting Health information system and data registration reviews and assessments, and the implementation of Data Quality Improvement plans and microplanning activities.
- Verifying health supplies are delivered to target beneficiaries in line with relevant programme documents and flag any delays and bottlenecks.
- Conducting post-distribution monitoring (PDM) of supplies to assess beneficiaries’ feedback in terms of the quality, timeliness and relevance of supplies delivered. Other end-user monitoring of specific programmes will be conducted as required by the Zonal Office.
- Collecting direct feedback form beneficiaries and affected population about the situation and needs, and the suitability of the services provided and how to improve.

DELIVERABLE(s)

- Provincial need assessment for implementation of mobile health teams completed
- Monthly monitoring of mobile health and nutrition teams service delivery points conducted.
- Monthly report of availability of ORS/Zinc stock with CHWs submitted
- Coordination, and monitoring of community mobilization/engagement activities facilitated
- Need assessment of CHWs training for target provinces completed
- Training of CHWs supported by our client monitored
- Routine EPI monitoring checklists completed and reported (this checklist includes all components of Routine EPI).
- Oriented on new RI activities e.g., accelerated immunization, Measles interventions, awareness raising activities (IEC, media broadcast, etc.).
- Percentage of HFs equipped with SDDs reported.
- Emergency need assessment of emergency affected areas completed
- Our client supported emergency activities monitored including HF under the Sahatmandi CERF support.
- Field visits implemented and reported timely with the required quality.
- Situation monitoring reports and needs assessment data is provided.
- Programme monitoring reports are developed and shared with zonal office programme officers\\specialists and reginal health extender including progress information, gaps and challenges, supplies monitoring, and beneficiaries’ feedback.
- Partner’s capacity in area of extender technical expertise is built.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Minimum Qualification and Experience:

- Having certificate in health, medicine, public health, nursing, midwife or related field.
- Minimum of 2 years of experience in in health, medicine, public health, nurse, midwife or related field.
- Proficiency in data analysis and interpretation.
- Excellent communication skills for effective collaboration with healthcare professionals and stakeholders.
- Proven ability to contribute to the enhancement of health programs through data-driven insights.
- Reporting skills

Team management

 This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role.

fields.title: Project Evaluation Consultant
fields.body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23684**  
Position Title: **Project Evaluation Consultant (Type B)**  
Duty Station City: **Port Vila**  
Duty Station Country: **Vanuatu**  
Contract Type: **Consultant B**  
*Recruiting Type:* **Consultancy**  
*Vacancy Type:* **Call for Applications**  
Initial duration: **2 months**  
Closing date: **03 November 2026**

**Context:**

Since 2015, more than 30 per cent of Ni-Vanuatu citizens have experienced temporary or protracted displacement due to disasters. Vanuatu's approximately 300,000 people (Vanuatu Bureau of Statistics, 2020) spread across 83 islands are exposed to cyclones, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, ashfalls, earthquakes, mudslides, flooding and drought. As the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events increases due to climate change, disasters pose a primary threat to Vanuatu's national security and human development.

Tropical Cyclones (TC) Judy and Kevin (both of Category 4 intensity) made landfall over Vanuatu on 1 and 3 March 2023. TC Judy and Kevin affected an estimated 24,657 households (123,288 people) with 90 per cent of houses in Shefa and Tafea provinces destroyed or severely damaged. The cumulative impact of compounding events such as previous cyclones (TC Harold), high La Nina rainfall and COVID-19, has had a devastating impact on basic living conditions, access to basic services, livelihoods, and coping capacities. While traditional resilience in Vanuatu is strong, emergency preparedness needs strengthening at all levels - national, provincial, area council and community – particularly in light of intensifying climate change impacts in the Pacific.

In response, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is implementing a project to support the Vanuatu National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) in strengthening the capacity of national and provincial government institutions, Community Disaster and Climate Change Committees (CDCCCs), Area Councils, faith-based organizations, and community leaders — particularly women leaders — to develop and maintain safe and dignified evacuation arrangements during emergencies.

This builds on the existing work being undertaken by the Displacement and Evacuation Centre Management (DECM) Cluster which brings together key partners to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities. It will strengthen and extend the work of the DECM Cluster to provincial and community level, moving towards improved localization of emergency response measures in Vanuatu.

Specifically, the Sef Ples Blong Yumi Phase 2 project funded by the Government of Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), implemented by the National Disaster Management Office, Vanuatu in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration, supports the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness, coordination, and evacuation centre management across multiple hazards. The project focuses on strengthening the DECM Cluster’s coordination capacity, updating and rolling out the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and Evacuation Toolbox / Training Materials, improving information management systems, and supporting preparedness at national, provincial, and Area Council levels.

**The Objective of the project is:**

To contribute to the protection and resilience of people at risk of displacement in Vanuatu by supporting the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness and evacuation procedures.

The project will update and finalize the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and developing the Evacuations Toolbox / Training Materials for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to strengthen:

1. National, provincial and area council-level coordination of evacuations.
2. Capacity of communities, CDCCCs, faith-based groups to manage and lead their own community-based evacuations in ways that both draws on traditional knowledge about evacuations and increases protections for vulnerable groups, especially women, children, older people and people with disability.

The Outcomes and Outputs of this project are the following:

Outcome 1: Government, faith-based groups and communities have enhanced capacity to coordinate, develop, maintain and monitor safe, dignified evacuation accommodation in emergencies.

Output 1.1: Improved information management at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in sudden-onset emergencies.

Output 1.2: Improved coordination at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in emergencies.

Output 1.3: Updated National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines and Evacuations Toolbox for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

Output 1.4: Roll out of Evacuations Toolbox training for national trainers, Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

Disaster Risk Reduction - Humanitarian

Project code: CC0083

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

**The Final Evaluation Report shall include the following sections:**

- Executive Summary
- Introduction, objectives, methodology, and limitations
- Findings (relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, sustainability and cross-cutting issues)
- Discussions of outcomes and results
- Lessons learned and good practices (success factors and/or those which challenged performance)
- Conclusions
- Recommendations
- Annexes (i.e. TOR, Data Sources, Evaluation Matrix, etc.)
- Further details of the deliverables are:
    
    **Other general tasks to be undertaken as part of this assignment will include**
- Providing advice and input to project direction and methods.
- Reporting to and keeping up good communication with National Programme Officer and Project Manager.
- Attendance at project meetings online or in person.
- Meetings, where requested, with IOM Chief of Mission, IOM Project Staff, or Government of Vanuatu representatives.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Performance should be assessed according to the tangible and measurable deliverables of the work assignment as stated in Section 7 above.
- Payment instalments to be made upon the satisfactory completion of each of the deliverables and approval by the project manager.
- Performance will be assessed against the outputs as provided above.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- The evaluator should preferably have a master's degree in political science, public policy, development, social science, government administration, climate change, sustainable development, refugee and migration studies, international relations, or related field from an accredited academic institution and 2 years of relevant professional experience.
- Or the evaluator should have a bachelors degree in political science, public policy, development, social science, government administration, climate change, sustainable development, refugee and migration studies, international relations, or related field from an accredited academic institution and 4 years of relevant professional experience.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in carrying out similar evaluation assignments for projects related to humanitarian preparedness, response, recovery, disaster resilience, climate change, evacuation center management, or displacement and evacuation center management coordination.
- Demonstrated capacity to coordinate with and secure key informants (including government actors, community networks, other key stakeholders, and community participants) is required.
- Minimum 4 years of experience working with research, policy development, analysis, monitoring and evaluation, and program evaluation preferably in the field of climate change, disaster risk reduction, emergency response, and / or environment.
- Understanding of Vanuatu displacement, emergency response, evacuation centres, and climate change context are an advantage
- Experience of working in the Pacific region is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Good communication and coordination skills.
- Computer skills required (MS Word and basic MS Excel) for reporting.
- Strong facilitation, mentoring, and stakeholder coordination skills.

**Languages**

- For this consultancy, Fluency in Bislama and English language is required. Working knowledge of French is an advantage.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required**

One trip to Port Vila will be required as part of this ToR:  
Trip 1: Approximately 10 days (estimated early - December 2026 or early January 2027) – this travel is required to coordinate evaluation activities, attend meetings, and conduct key informant interviews. Exact dates of the trip to be coordinated between IOM Project Management Team and the selected evaluator(s).  
If budget allows a second trip can be considered in mid or late January 2027.  
IOM will cover costs relating to round trip airfares, accommodation, and a consultant / evaluator daily subsistence allowance. Travel and health insurance will not be covered by IOM and is the responsibility of the consultant / selected evaluator(s).

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at [this link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Notes**

fields.title: MEAL Coordinator (MEAL Advisor) - Caracas
fields.body:
The Danish Refugee Council is one of the world's leading humanitarian NGOs, working in over 30 countries to provide adequate assistance and protection to refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, returnees, people on the move, and vulnerable local populations/host communities. Currently, DRC is seeking a highly qualified national o International **MEAL Coordinator (MEAL Advisor)** based in Caracas, Venezuela.

**About the job:** DRC is managing its operations in Venezuela under the direction of the country office in Caracas and four field offices located in the states of Sucre, Apure, and Zulia (Maracaibo and Santa Barbara de Zulia). DRC Venezuela is implementing an integrated Action encompassing the Protection, Food Security & Livelihood, WASH and Disaster Preparedness sectors.

**The overall purpose of the role**:

The MEAL Coordinator provides country-level technical advice and capacity strengthening to support the development of DRC Venezuela’s Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning function. Under the supervision of the Head of Programmes, the role works closely with the existing MEAL leadership, MEAL staff, programme teams and partners to strengthen practical systems, improve the quality and use of evidence, and support accountable programming across emergency response, recovery and longer-term interventions.

The role supports a collaborative review of MEAL capacities, systems and ways of working, translates findings into a prioritised improvement plan, and accompanies its implementation through mentoring, coaching and hands-on technical support. The Coordinator promotes sustainable approaches adapted to country needs and team capacities, in line with DRC’s Global MEAL Model and donor requirements.

The position provides advisory and technical coordination support. The existing MEAL leadership retains responsibility for departmental management and day-to-day delivery. Priorities and recommendations are agreed with the Head of Programmes in consultation with relevant colleagues.

**Responsibilities:**

**MEAL development and technical advisory support**

- Facilitate a participatory review of MEAL systems, staffing capacities, workflows, tools and coordination arrangements, recognising existing strengths and identifying opportunities for improvement.
- Review how MEAL commitments are translated into workplans and delivered across country and field offices, including the factors affecting timeliness, data quality and utilisation of findings.
- Develop an achievable MEAL strengthening plan with the existing MEAL leadership and Head of Programmes, with clear priorities, responsibilities, timelines and measures of progress.
- Advise on the country MEAL strategy, departmental workplan, resourcing and division of responsibilities between MEAL, programme teams and partners.
- Provide regular, evidence-based recommendations to the Head of Programmes and support follow-up on agreed improvement actions.

**Capacity strengthening and accompaniment**

- Identify learning needs jointly with MEAL and programme staff and develop a tailored capacity-building plan covering country and field teams.
- Provide structured mentoring, coaching and practical support to MEAL leadership and staff, including through joint field visits and review of actual project tools and outputs.
- Facilitate practical learning sessions on MEAL planning, indicator design, sampling, mixed methods, data analysis, accountability and communication of findings.
- Develop accessible guidance and reusable resources and support their consistent application across offices.
- Assess the application of learning in practice and progressively transfer strengthened tools and processes to the responsible teams.

**Results monitoring and programme quality support**

- Support the integration of MEAL throughout Project Cycle Management, including proposals, grant opening, periodic reviews and close-out.
- Advise on theories of change, logframes, indicators, MEAL plans and realistic MEAL budgets, in collaboration with technical coordinators and grants colleagues.
- Review and strengthen indicator tracking tables, means of verification and reporting processes to improve consistency, completeness and timely consolidation.
- Support the design and refinement of context-appropriate quantitative and qualitative data collection methods for assessments, baselines, monitoring and outcome measurement.
- Provide technical quality assurance for sampling, data collection, data entry, analysis and reporting, and support resolution of recurrent bottlenecks.
- Work with relevant colleagues to strengthen data protection, secure storage, responsible sharing and practical use of digital collection and visualisation tools.

**Accountability to affected populations**

- Support MEAL and programme teams in strengthening accessible, inclusive and safe community feedback mechanisms and information provision.
- Review feedback workflows and advise on timely handling, appropriate referral of sensitive complaints and closure of the feedback loop, in line with DRC procedures.
- Build staff capacities on accountability, ethical data collection and Core Humanitarian Standard commitments.
- Support regular analysis of feedback trends and their use in programme reviews and decision-making.

**Evaluation analysis and learning**

- Advise on evaluation and research planning, methodologies and terms of reference in line with DRC policy and donor requirements.
- Support the analysis and interpretation of monitoring and evaluation findings and their translation into practical programme recommendations.
- Facilitate learning reviews and reflection sessions across teams and partners, documenting lessons and following up agreed actions.
- Support the preparation of clear evidence products and presentation of key findings to programme teams and senior management.

**Partner support and coordination**

- Work with partnership and MEAL colleagues to assess partner capacities and agree proportionate monitoring, reporting and accountability arrangements.
- Provide targeted technical support and capacity building to partners and facilitate joint learning and harmonisation of tools where appropriate.
- Coordinate technical exchanges across country and field offices and with relevant DRC global MEAL counterparts.
- Represent DRC in relevant technical coordination forums when delegated by the Head of Programmes.
- Perform other relevant duties assigned by the Head of Programmes within the scope of the role.

**Experience and technical competencies**

- Minimum five years of relevant MEAL experience in humanitarian or development programmes, including country-level technical coordination or advisory responsibilities.
- Demonstrated experience strengthening existing MEAL departments or systems through collaborative assessment, prioritised improvement planning and sustained technical support.
- Proven mentoring, coaching and facilitation skills, including experience supporting national staff and working effectively through technical influence and collaborative relationships.
- Strong practical knowledge of theories of change, logframes, indicator design, sampling, quantitative and qualitative methods, data quality assurance and evaluations.
- Experience translating data and community feedback into programme improvements and organisational learning.
- Experience with accountability mechanisms, CHS, ethical research and data protection in humanitarian settings.
- Advanced Excel skills and experience with digital data collection tools such as KoboToolbox or ODK; experience with Power BI or statistical analysis software is an asset.
- Experience meeting institutional donor MEAL requirements and supporting local partners.
- Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to propose practical solutions and support constructive dialogue.
- Previous experience with DRC systems, Latin American contexts or emergency response is an asset.

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, social sciences, statistics, research, public health or another relevant discipline
- A relevant postgraduate qualification or specialised training in MEAL is an asset.

**Languages**

- Full professional proficiency in Spanish and English, spoken and written.

**We offer:**

- The opportunity to be part of one of the best NGOs worldwide.
- Access to over 1,000 free online trainings and certifications.
- Contract duration: subject to budget availability.
- Salary: Band G / Terms of Employment for national or expatriate staff, as applicable
- HCM insurance fully covered by the organization.

**DRC Core Competencies:**

- Achieving Excellence: Focus on achieving results and ensuring efficient processes.
- Collaboration: Engage relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- Taking the Initiative: Take ownership and initiative while seeking innovation.
- Communicating: Listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- Demonstrating Integrity: Act in accordance with DRC's vision and values.

**Application Process:** All applicants must upload a cover letter (max. 1 page) and an updated CV (max. 2 pages, without attachments) in English or Spanish, on the DRC employment platform. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

**Application Deadline:** Sunday, november 01 at 11:59 pm Local Time. Please note that applications will be reviewed continuously, and interviews will be scheduled as soon as a suitable candidate is identified. DRC reserves the right to close the vacancy before the deadline once a suitable candidate is identified.

**Start Date:** November 2026

fields.title: Qualitative Research Expert
fields.body:
**Position:** Qualitative Research Expert (Consultancy)

**Company:** Aflatoun International

**Location:** West Kalimantan, Indonesia

**Consultancy fee:** TBD

**Application deadline:** 25 October 2026, 5:00 pm CET

**Background information**

**Aflatoun International**

Aflatoun International is a non-profit organization, which offers social, financial & entrepreneurship education to children and young people worldwide, empowering them to make a positive change for a more equitable world. Aflatoun creates high-quality curricula for different age groups, which are contextualized to local needs and circumstances, and are implemented by over 300 partner organizations in 101 countries. By using a social franchise model, Aflatoun transfers curricular content, monitoring and evaluation tools, and training capacity to partner organisations, helping them enhance their existing expertise and create an efficient learning ecosystem. Aflatoun’s programmes follow an active-learning, participant-centred methodology, which combines social and financial education (SFE) through engaging participants, educators, government institutions and civil society organisations.

**The program**

Aflatoun International has developed Financial Literacy Module (FLM) for parents aiming to improve parents' and caregivers' financial knowledge and financial health, enabling them to provide responsive and nurturing care for their children. In Indonesia, the programme reached more than 2300 parents/caregivers and 3300 children. Understanding various challenges faced by parents and caregivers, and whether and how the program has helped them overcome these challenges will provide valuable insights on the beneficiaries’ experience of the program.

**Scope of the work**

We are seeking a qualitative research consultant to produce an article that captures the beliefs, experiences, and challenges related to the financial lives of our program participants in Indonesia. Consultant will prepare a field work plan with an interview guide, conduct in-person and remote interviews at the location, transcribe and analyse the data, and deliver the article. Where possible, the consultant will combine storytelling with in-field observations, photography, or any other method to enrich the information and complement the narrative. The length of the article is about 3,000 words.

The final article should:

1. Detail the challenges that participants may face (especially financial challenges affecting parenting and well-being of children) in the local and regional context.
2. Detail how the program was implemented from the perspective of both the program implementers and the participants.
3. Describe the relevance of the program content and the extent to which it addresses the participants' challenges, in a human-centred narrative format.

We are looking for a candidate based in Indonesia who can travel to and work in West Kalimantan, Indonesia. The candidate must be available to travel three consecutive days to the fieldwork location in November or December (exact dates to be decided).

**Deliverables**

1. **Develop the storytelling interview structure:** Based on discussions with Aflatoun’s program implementation team and M&E team (online), develop the field work plan with an interview guide.

Number of days: 0.5

1. **Identify the groups/individuals for conducting interviews:** Together with Aflatoun and the implementing NGOs, identify the groups or individuals to interview.

Number of days: 0.5

1. **Coordinate the logistics:** Coordinate own travel (transportation and accommodation if necessary) to conduct the storytelling activity upon approval from Aflatoun.

Number of days: 1

1. **Fieldwork/interviews at the location:** Conduct qualitative data collection with the agreed approach (in-person interviews and observation).

Number of days: 3

1. **Remote interviews with partner NGOs:** Conduct remote interviews with 2-3 partner organisations in Indonesia

Number of days: 1

1. **Transcribe and analyse interview data:** Transcribe, clean, organize and analyse the collected data it in a shareable format.

Number of days: 2

1. **Final article:** Draft the final article based on the scope of work and share it with Aflatoun. Revise the article after review where necessary.

Number of days: 4

Total: **12 days**

**Required Skills & Qualifications**

- Academic qualification in Development Studies, Anthropology, Social Sciences or related field.
- Strong skills and experience in conducting qualitative research, focus group discussions, storytelling, and report writing.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Analytical, critical thinking and strong problem-solving skills.
- Fluent in written and spoken English and Bahasa Indonesian.
- Ability to work effectively in a small team with an international environment.
- Computer skills, including sound knowledge of Windows and Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Graphic and/video editing is a plus.
- Familiarity with topics in financial education/financial literacy, and the local contexts is a plus.
- The consultant must be able to conduct fieldwork and in-person interviews in West Kalimantan.

**Payment Schedule**

The payment for 100% of the contract will be made upon submission and approval of the final article attached with the transcription and analysis (deliverables 6 and 7).

**Hiring Details**

The position is for a Consultancy. We offer a dynamic and pleasant multicultural working environment. Due to the nature of Aflatoun’s work with children around the world, specific attention is drawn towards Aflatoun’s Child Protection Policy and its Policy on the Protection of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). These two policies are required to be signed by consultants and forms part of the consultancy contract. The applicant commits to zero tolerance towards sexual exploitation and abuse.

Screening for integrity is part of the recruitment process. Aflatoun considers it important to ensure the reliability, professionalism and the Integrity of its organization and its team. By applying for this position, the candidate accepts to be screened by Aflatoun which involves conducting a background check with 2 referees from the professional environment of the candidate, submitting a self-declaration of good conduct along with the CV and cover letter, and submitting a declaration of good conduct issued by the Judicial Documentation system in their home country in case they reach the final stage of the hiring process. The screening will cover up to 10 years. Only the data relevant for the screening of the position will be collected. In case the candidate is not selected for the position, the data will be destroyed 4 weeks after the closing of the position. For technical positions, an additional written test may be required.

fields.title: Security Advisory – Journalist protection - West Asia
fields.body:
MiCT is calling for proposals for freelance Security Advisory services in the framework of its program “MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices 2026-2027” in West Asia, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. This will be a service contract, running from November 2026 - June 2027. MiCT invites interested and qualified people and /or organisations to submit proposals by 1.11.2026.

**Introducing MiCT:**

Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) is a non-profit organisation delivering expert media services in complex and challenging contexts with passion, precision, and agility.

Through collaborative work with partners, MiCT fosters transparent, inclusive, and fair dialogue supporting resilient societies. Operating across three continents and 15 countries, MiCT facilitates journalist training, media content production, research, monitoring, and supports the financial sustainability of media partners.

**About the Project:**

Since 2022, the MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices has supported at-risk journalists and media professionals from conflict regions, enabling them to continue their essential work in safety. The programme is part of the Hannah Arendt Initiative and a member of the Journalists in Distress Network. It offers stipends, security and equipment support, (mental) health services, legal aid, relocation, and professional development through regional hubs.

**Description of the role:**

To support the Fellows from West Asia, MiCT is looking to provide support and guidance on security matters through trainings, risk assessments and one-on-one mentorship sessions. The focus areas will include, but are not limited to, advanced digital security, identifying, mitigating and responding to digital threats, preventive and responsive protection mechanisms, identifying digital attacks, secure communication, device and data protection, risk mitigation strategies, and individualized support to Fellows facing security threats. The contract will run from November 2026 until June 2027.

The risk assessments should give a comprehensive overview of the person’s security situation, covering digital and/or physical security as required, and providing concrete and prioritised next steps. Any additional mentoring sessions will be agreed upon in writing following the finalisation of the needs assessment.

**Application Requirements**

Successful applicants should be able to provide proof of the following:

- Minimum of 5 years of experience in security risk management in West Asia.
- Strong understanding of the media and security landscape in West Asia.
- Experience working with journalists in crisis and conflict contexts.
- Proven experience in conducting individual risk assessments and crisis management.
- Ability to develop and deliver security training and one-on-one consultancy.
- Excellent communication skills and ability to work with diverse teams.
- Fluency in Arabic is a must. Fluency in English is preferred.
- Flexibility and teamwork.

fields.title: Officer, M/E
fields.body:
**JOB SUMMARY**

The role of the Officer Monitoring and Evaluation (M/E) is to implement the M/E work plan and contribute to achieving and improving the quality of the program/project. The Officer M/E will provide support by collecting and managing the program's/project's output and outcome data. Officer M/E also plays a key role in data analysis and carrying out M/E activities in the field. The Officer M/E will provide support to the program’s M/E function in the field through working closely with the field staff to ensure the quality of the program/project.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation.

**MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**IMC’s policies, guidelines, and procedures**

- Mainstream the Global M/E Guidelines across all related M/E activities at the field level and ensure the guidance notes for monitoring and evaluation are functional at the field level.
- Apply and adapt existing Global M/E Guidelines, tools, and templates at the relevant stages of the project cycle.
- Actively promote the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) standards within IMC and amongst its beneficiaries.
- Contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of the Code of Conduct, ethics, values, and standpoint with regards to internal and external actors.

**Project design and planning**

- Participate in needs assessments by organizing the training for enumerators on assessment methodology, tools, respondent’s selection, and supervise field team to ensure field level data integrity.
- Ensure that M/E activities are participatory.
- Support in developing results framework and log frame, including indicators, for simple projects.

**M/E system**

- Ensure that different components of the M/E system are functional and relevant and maintain IPTT to track output, outcome, and impact indicators and their measurement in the different sectors of relevance.
- Support M/E department in development of databases for all programs by using available technologies.
- Organize and lead data collection activities following the data collection and reporting flow put in place for a project.
- Use tools for tracking project's progress and bottlenecks and develop simple data collection tools based on monitoring indicators.
- Maintain effective M/E system (ensure data collected translates to the M/E Framework/IPTT).
- Conduct regular field visits.
- Conduct periodic data analysis and triangulate data from other M/E exercises.

**Data quality management**

- Conduct periodic data quality audits to assess the quality of collected data for indicators.
- Mitigate data pitfalls, issues, and ensure that strategies for quality data are in place.
- Report data quality issues to the M/E Manager/Coordinator.
- Adhere to the fundamental concepts of data quality.
- Conduct on-site routine data quality audits at community levels.
- Assess the quality of collected data for indicators.
- Provide supportive supervision on data quality at facility and community-levels.

**Sampling**

- Implement probability and non-probability sampling techniques as and when appropriate after consulting with manager.
- Develop sampling frame and carry out sampling following instructions (manager, guidelines).

**Qualitative and quantitative techniques**

- Use different qualitative and quantitative methods of data collection including structured/semi structured interviews, key informant interviews, in-depth interviews, group discussions, focus group discussions and direct observations as an M/E tool.
- Conduct trainings on qualitative techniques for data collection for M/E staff, program staff, and interviewers.
- Develop and use key qualitative tools (observation checklists, guide for group discussion and interviews) for monitoring purposes.
- Apply the different interview techniques (structured/semi-structured) and use appropriate questionnaires for monitoring purposes as and when appropriate
- Conduct regular and ad-hoc (when required) site visits to monitor data collection processes to ensure data quality.

**Mobile and manual data collection**

- Determine the appropriate data collection tool based on the purpose, advantages and disadvantages of mobile data collection techniques.
- Install and configure mobile data collection tools (OKD collect, Kobo collect, ONA collect, etc.) on smart phones or tablets
- Design simple questionnaire using XLS form and configure mobile phones and tablets for mobile data collection.
- Use smart phones/tablets for data collection
- Provide training to M/E staff and enumerators on mobile data collection mechanisms and software, and provide technical support and troubleshooting during all stages of mobile data collection, ensuring data is transferred from mobile devices and the devices are securely stored (sign in/sign out system for enumerators) and ensuring devices are charged
- Data analysis, including use of statistical software
- Perform data cleaning and ensuring data integrity before data analysis.
- Organizing and overseeing data entry and data consolidation.
- Perform descriptive univariate and bivariate data analysis using Excel Pivot tables or statistical software.
- Interpret frequency tables, bi-variate cross tables, the mean and median.

**Evaluation design**

- Contribute to the preparation of project evaluation and facilitating the field level work.
- Use and supervise quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods of data collection in evaluation.

**Techniques for presenting information**

- Communicate clearly the findings of monitoring activities and reviews against targets set by the project.
- Compile data and indicators at the project's level for reporting in a clear and concise manner, providing all required information.
- Develop information products to share results of data analysis and monitoring.
- Drafting reports of assessments and surveys

**Knowledge Management and Learning**

- Organize the documentation of the project's M/E activities, results, and processes.
- Organize secondary data (internal and external sources).

**Cross-cutting themes**

- Monitor the general context through regular field visits and report issues affecting beneficiaries and intra-community relations.
- Ensure data collected is representative of population and demonstrate an understanding of social dynamics.
- Document the needs of target populations, including people of different sex, age, and vulnerability status, into all M/E systems and activities.
- Support or lead in the implementation of analyses and assessments of the impact of sex on outcomes, as required, including staff capacity building on tools and protocols; data collection; data analysis; and report writing.
- Ensure tools and systems are in place for learning and decision making on the needs of crisis-affected groups, including disaggregation of all data, development of mainstreamed and specific indicators, specific research questions, and targeted recommendations in reports

Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- Typically, bachelor’s degree in social sciences, public health, statistics, or international development, with experience in M/E. Equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.
- Typically, 3+ years of relevant and progressive experience with a humanitarian organization in implementing and overseeing monitoring and evaluation systems.
- Knowledge of data pitfalls, issues, and strategies for assessing the quality of collected data.
- Knowledge of commonly used probability and purposive sampling techniques and different methods of qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis.
- Knowledge of descriptive univariate and bivariate data analysis using Excel Pivot tables or other advanced analysis software.
- Knowledge of indicators and their measurement in the different sectors of relevance.
- Understand the concept of participatory monitoring, evaluation and needs assessment.
- Excellent proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
- Strong training facilitator/presentation skills.
- Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
- Have analytical, conceptual, and strategic thinking skills.
- Manage performance by setting clear goals.
- High-level English proficiency (Speaking – Reading – Writing)
- High-level MISSION’S LANGUAGE proficiency (Speaking – Reading – Writing).
- Travel: 0-25%

**Ethical Conduct at International Medical Corps**

As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our *Code of Conduct and Ethics* and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our *Code of Conduct and Ethics*, including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships.

International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the *Code of Conduct and Ethics,* all staffare required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our *Code of Conduct and Ethics* and *Whistleblower Policy* prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

**Equal Opportunities**

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

fields.title: 23246 Programme Officer (Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)) (P)
fields.body:
Launched in August 2021 with funding from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the Better Regional Migration Management (BRMM) Programme is IOM’s flagship labour migration programme in the East and Horn of Africa (EHOA). The programme supports efforts to strengthen labour migration governance, promote fair and ethical recruitment, enhance the protection of migrant workers and their families, and expand access to safe, orderly and regular labour migration pathways. Building on earlier phases, the current BRMM FY26–27 framework focuses on operationalising skills-to-employment, skills mobility and ethical recruitment systems for safe labour migration in the EHOA. It prioritises scalable and evidence-based interventions that improve access to decent work, strengthen national and regional labour migration systems, and contribute to reducing reliance on irregular migration routes. The programme will be implemented in four priority countries—Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia and Uganda—while continuing to support regional cooperation through the Regional Ministerial Forum on Migration (RMFM), Regional Economic Communities and relevant national institutions. It places particular emphasis on vulnerable groups, including youth, women, returnees, refugees and migrant workers, and supports interventions related to labour market information systems, public employment services, skills development and recognition, bilateral labour migration agreements, ethical recruitment, migrant protection, reintegration and engagement with countries of destination, including the Gulf States. A strong monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning approach, together with communication and visibility efforts, will support adaptive management, donor accountability and the documentation of results and lessons learned.

Under the overall supervision of the EHOA Regional Director and direct supervision of the Regional Program Management Officer, Labour Mobility and Human Development, the Programme Officer (Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)) will be responsible for the implementation of the M&E aspects of the BRMM program in line with the expectations of the donors.

**Responsibilities**

1. Lead and be responsible for the overall Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) function of the BRMM project, including the development, updating and implementation of the project M&E plan, results framework, data collection tools, quality assurance mechanisms and monitoring procedures.
2. Provide regular technical M&E support to implementing missions, including guidance on data collection, activity monitoring, results tracking, reporting requirements, data quality and the accurate reflection of M&E plans in mission-level action plans.
3. Lead the collection, consolidation, analysis and use of BRMM project monitoring data to track progress against agreed indicators, inform programme decisions, identify implementation gaps and ensure that programme-related datasets are accurate and up to date.
4. Prepare BRMM biannual and annual reports by compiling, verifying and analysing inputs from implementing missions, ensuring that reported results are evidence-based, consistent with donor requirements and aligned with the project results framework.
5. Review and provide technical guidance on activity concept notes, mission activity reports and related workplans, ensuring that M&E requirements, indicators, targets, verification methods and follow-up actions are clearly and accurately reflected.
6. Undertake monitoring visits to implementing missions, as required, to assess progress, verify reported results, support corrective actions and provide hands-on guidance on the implementation of BRMM M&E processes.
7. Design, coordinate and conduct surveys, outcome monitoring exercises, impact assessments and other learning or evidence-generation activities when required by programme needs or requested by the donor.
8. Support adaptive management, learning and accountability by tracking risks, assumptions, lessons learned and emerging results; ensuring responsible data management; and providing evidence-based recommendations to improve BRMM implementation, reporting and donor accountability.
9. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Statistics, Economics, Public Policy, Migration Studies, International Relations, Law, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.
- Specific training or certification in Monitoring and Evaluation, Results-Based Management, data analysis, research methods, or impact assessment would be an advantage.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in leading Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) functions for complex projects, including the development and implementation of M&E plans, results frameworks, indicators, data collection tools, quality assurance mechanisms and monitoring procedures;
- Demonstrated experience in Project Cycle Management (PCM), Results-Based Management (RBM), monitoring data collection, consolidation, analysis and use of evidence to inform programme implementation, reporting and adaptive management;
- Experience in providing technical M&E support to implementing missions or field teams, including guidance on activity monitoring, results tracking, data quality, reporting requirements and the integration of M&E plans into action plans;
- Experience in preparing high-quality donor reports, including biannual and annual reports, by compiling, verifying and analysing inputs from implementing partners or missions and ensuring alignment with results frameworks and donor requirements;
- Experience in reviewing activity concept notes, activity reports, workplans and related documentation to ensure that M&E requirements, indicators, targets, verification methods, risks, assumptions and follow-up actions are clearly reflected;
- Experience in conducting monitoring visits, surveys, outcome monitoring exercises, evaluations, impact assessments or other evidence-generation activities to assess progress, verify results and support programme learning;
- Experience in maintaining programme datasets, ensuring responsible data management and producing evidence-based recommendations to strengthen implementation, accountability, learning and donor reporting; and,
- Experience in labour migration, migrant protection, ethical recruitment, bilateral labour migration agreements, skills mobility or related migration governance programming would be an advantage.

**Skills**

- Strong communication and coordination skills, including the ability to present M&E findings clearly, provide practical guidance to implementing missions, and communicate evidence-based recommendations to programme teams, management and donors;
- Strong analytical skills, including the ability to collect, verify, consolidate and interpret quantitative and qualitative data for reporting, learning and decision-making;
- Excellent report-writing skills, including the ability to prepare evidence-based donor, biannual and annual reports aligned with results frameworks and reporting requirements;
- Ability to provide technical M&E guidance and capacity support to implementing missions, including on activity monitoring, data quality, reporting and the integration of M&E requirements into concept notes and action plans; and,
- Ability to conduct monitoring visits, surveys, outcome monitoring, impact assessments and learning exercises to support adaptive management and donor accountability.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) or a relevant EHoA languages is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

## Project Overview

Accordemy® is seeking an experienced GIS trainer and consultant to deliver a two-day, in-person professional development program titled **"The Use of GIS in Humanitarian Projects"** in Madrid, Spain.

The program aims to strengthen participants' ability to apply Geographic Information Systems (GIS) in humanitarian operations, project planning, land and asset management, risk assessment, and evidence-based decision-making.

The training should emphasize practical applications, real-world scenarios, and the effective use of geospatial information to support humanitarian project implementation and management.

## Proposed Training Topics

The program is expected to cover:

1. **GIS Applications in Humanitarian Projects** — GIS for humanitarian planning, coordination, needs assessment, and operational management.
2. **Geospatial Data Collection and Management** — Spatial datasets, data integration, mapping layers, and geographic information management.
3. **Spatial Analysis and Risk Assessment** — Identifying vulnerable areas, assessing geographic risks, and supporting project prioritization.
4. **Land and Asset Mapping** — Mapping land parcels, infrastructure, resources, and project-affected locations.
5. **GIS for Evidence-Based Decision-Making** — Spatial suitability assessment, comparison of alternatives, and management decision support.
6. **GIS Visualization and Reporting** — Thematic maps, dashboards, analytical outputs, and communicating geographic findings to stakeholders.
7. **AI Integration with GIS** — Practical applications of artificial intelligence, automation, and emerging geospatial technologies.
8. **GIS Data Security and Stakeholder Information Management** — Data privacy, access control, secure sharing, and responsible management of sensitive geographic information.
9. **Practical GIS Exercises** — Hands-on demonstrations and case studies relevant to humanitarian and development projects.

The final training outline will be agreed upon with the selected consultant, considering their technical expertise and recommendations.

## Consultant Qualifications

Candidates should demonstrate:

- Strong professional experience in Geographic Information Systems and spatial analysis.
- **Proficiency in ArcGIS and proven experience teaching or delivering professional training using ArcGIS.**
- Experience designing and delivering instructor-led GIS training programs.
- Ability to explain technical GIS concepts clearly to professionals and managers.
- Practical knowledge of GIS applications in humanitarian assistance, international development, land management, or related fields.
- Familiarity with AI-assisted geospatial analysis and GIS data management practices.
- Excellent English communication and presentation skills.
- Availability to deliver the training in person in Madrid on the specified dates.

Experience working with humanitarian organizations, development agencies, NGOs, or international institutions would be an advantage.

## Expected Deliverables

- A finalized two-day training outline.
- Instructor-led delivery with practical demonstrations.
- Relevant training presentations, exercises, and example datasets.
- Hands-on activities that allow participants to apply the concepts.
- Supporting technical reference materials, where appropriate./

fields.title: External Endline Evaluation Consultancy for Promoting Access to Water and Education (PAWE) Project Mandera County.
fields.body:
**Terms of Reference**

**External Endline Evaluation Consultancy**

**Promoting Access to Water and Education (PAWE) Project Mandera County**

**IRK/PAWE/CONSUL/002/10/2026**

**ISSUED ON: Friday, 16th October 2026**

**CLOSING DATE: Thursday, 22nd October 2026 at 11:00 AM**

**October, 2026**

**Project: Promoting Access to Water and Education (PAWE) Project**  
**Activity: External Endline Evaluation**  
**Location: Mandera County**  
**Duration: 28 days**

**1.0 BACKGROUND**  
IR Kenya started operations in Kenya in 1993 through a local CBO in Mandera District, Northern Kenya. It opened its fully-fledged office in March 2006 at the height of the drought in the Horn of Africa. Since then, it has been providing humanitarian and development assistance to vulnerable communities. Over these years, IRK has remarkably changed the lives of the vulnerable and disadvantaged communities. In January 2010 and October 2011, IRK extended its operation to Wajir County and Garissa County, to serve both the local community and refugees at Dadaab Camp. Islamic Relief Kenya is currently implementing programmes in the following sectors: Health and Nutrition; WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene); Sustainable Livelihoods and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR); Child Welfare/Protection & Education; and Emergency Response. Over the years, IR Kenya has implemented various development and relief activities which have remarkably changed the lives of vulnerable and disadvantaged communities in Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Kilifi, Marsabit, Tana River and Kajiado Counties.  
IR Kenya commits to standards which ascribe to program quality and improved programming. This obliges us to conduct an end-line evaluation study for PAWE Project – Mandera County, focusing on the specific areas of the project interventions to document intended and unintended changes that can be attributed to the project.  
**2.0 PROJECT SUMMARY**  
The Promoting Access to Water and Education (PAWE) Project is an 18-month integrated community support initiative implemented by Islamic Relief Kenya (IRK) in Mandera County. The project aims to empower vulnerable communities by addressing critical gaps in Education and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH). It seeks to improve access to inclusive, safe and accessible education for children while increasing the availability of clean and potable water for households, schools and food production, thereby contributing to improved well-being and resilience among targeted communities.  
The project combines infrastructure development with service improvement and capacity strengthening. Key interventions include the construction and rehabilitation of school infrastructure and boreholes, provision of education and learning materials, improvement of school WASH facilities, and installation of solar-powered water systems and associated infrastructure. Sustainability and community ownership are embedded in the project through capacity building of beneficiaries and relevant community structures, alongside active engagement of government departments at national, county and sub-county levels in the monitoring and technical supervision of Education and WASH interventions. The project is aligned with the Mandera County Integrated Development Plan (CIDP) 2023–2027, IR Kenya's strategic priorities, and relevant NDMA plans.  
Project goal/impact: Improved learning outcomes for children and enhanced access to clean, potable water for households in Mandera County  
Project outcomes:  
**Outcome 1:** Improved education facilities and materials for schools in Mandera County  
**Outcome 2:** Increased access to potable water for targeted households and schools  
Project outputs:  
**Output 1.1:** 1500 pupils have access to quality education  
**Output 2.1:** 3,000 households and 2 schools have access to clean portable water for household and livestock use  
**3.0 Purpose and Objectives of The Endline Evaluation**  
As the project approaches completion, IRK seeks to engage a qualified consultant/consultancy firm to conduct an independent external endline evaluation which will assess the extent to which the PAWE Project has achieved its intended objectives, outcomes and results against the established baseline and results framework. The evaluation will examine the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of the interventions, identify intended and unintended results, and document key achievements, challenges, good practices and lessons learned. The findings and recommendations will support accountability to project rightsholders and stakeholders and provide evidence to inform the design and implementation of future integrated Education and WASH programming by IRK.  
**4.0 Evaluation Scope**  
The evaluation will assess the overall performance, results and sustainability of the 18-month PAWE Project, with particular focus on the following areas:  
1\. Implementation and achievement of results across the project’s key thematic areas of Education and WASH, including the extent to which planned outputs, outcomes and objectives were achieved against the project results framework and baseline findings.  
2\. Relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of the project interventions, including the extent to which they responded to the priority needs of targeted communities and the likelihood that benefits will continue beyond the project period.  
3\. Quality and functionality of project-supported infrastructure and services, including constructed or rehabilitated education facilities, WASH facilities, boreholes, solar-powered water systems and other associated infrastructure.  
4\. Community perspectives and satisfaction regarding the relevance, timeliness, appropriateness, quality and adequacy of the assistance and services provided, including perceived changes resulting from the project.  
5\. Cross-cutting considerations, including gender, disability and social inclusion, safeguarding, protection, conflict sensitivity and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), with particular attention to equitable access and participation of vulnerable and marginalized groups.  
6\. Effectiveness, accessibility, confidentiality and perceived safety of IRK's feedback and complaints mechanisms, including community awareness and utilization of available channels and the extent to which feedback was received, responded to and used to improve implementation.  
7\. Community ownership, institutional capacity and sustainability, including the effectiveness of capacity-building initiatives, participation of community structures, and engagement of relevant county and sub-county government departments in monitoring, management and continued support of project interventions.  
8\. Key lessons, good practices, challenges and unintended results arising from implementation, with practical and actionable recommendations to strengthen the design and delivery of future integrated Education and WASH programmes.  
**5.0 Methodology**  
The consultants will propose the most suitable study design, sampling methods and approach, sample size, data collection, and analysis approaches that are suitable for this project at the endline. This should be clearly outlined in the bidding document/proposal, and if qualified, at the interview stage, to have further discussion with the evaluation management team. The consulting team should propose respondents' interviews or data sources that can answer the log frame indicators and provide comparable statistics (meaningful comparison between baseline/needs assessment and endline) to document any changes.  
**6.0 Expected Deliverables**  
The following are the expected deliverables.  
1\. Inception report and data collection tools.  
2\. Draft report to be validated by the Islamic Relief Kenya and Islamic Relief Worldwide technical team.  
3\. Final Report after addressing inputs from both IRK and IRW technical teams (the report must be submitted in MS Word and PDF format as well as three printed copies, which should be handed to the IRK team upon completion of this activity).  
4\. Datasets for quantitative data in Excel format and KII and FGD transcripts in Word. Beneficiary data is personal data and MUST be protected within the IRK data protection policy, which will be shared with the consultant.  
5\. A PowerPoint presentation which summarises the entire study  
In performing the activities related to the evaluation, the consultant is expected to strictly adhere to IRK, data protection and privacy policy, Child safeguarding, and the IRK code of conduct.  
**7.0 Roles and Responsibilities**  
**Role/Responsibilities of the Consultant**  
• Develop an inception report detailing the study design, methodology, indicators, data collection tools, and work plan schedule for carrying out the assignment agreed in consultation with the MEAL coordinator  
• Conduct a desk review of relevant project documents  
• Develop quantitative and qualitative data collection tools in consultation with the MEAL Coordinator  
• Conduct training for the data collection teams, including pre‐testing/piloting of tools  
• Plan and coordinate quantitative and qualitative data collection  
• Work with the IR Kenya project team in planning study logistics  
• Conduct data quality assurance  
• Review, clean, and analyze data collected  
• Presentation of the preliminary findings for input from the IRK team and stakeholders  
• Incorporate input from project stakeholders and submit a final report  
• Produce Endline study report  
**Role of IRK**  
• Recruit an external consultant for the endline study  
• Review and provide input on the consultant’s deliverables  
• Guide on the engagement with the consultant  
• Provide consultants with background documents, reports and available secondary data for review  
• Provide oversight during data collection  
• Ensure smooth flow of consultancy engagement processes, including all contractual obligations  
Reporting  
The consultant will report to the MEAL Coordinator and work closely with the IRK Mandera field office -Field Coordinator, MEAL and other project staff. The Project staff will support the coordination of the data collection process.  
**8.0 Duration of the Assignment and Logistics**  
The consultant should describe the evaluation’s overall schedule (i.e., duration, phasing, and timing of different activities), required preparations for work, conditions that might affect data collection, analysis and reporting. However, below are some suggested timelines owed to the urgency of this assignment and are open for deliberation.  
**ITEM # of days to complete Suggested dates**  
Selection of the consultant -  
Inception meeting between IR Kenya and the consultant to discuss the understanding of the assignment **1**  
Review of project documents and submission of the inception report, including data collection tools **5**  
Finalize the inception report and data collection tools based on feedback received **3**  
Planning & actualization of consultancy logistics **2**  
Conduct training for enumerators, including pre-testing and preparing for fieldwork **2**  
Conduct data collection **6**  
Data cleaning, analysis and submission of data tables and syntax files **3**  
Developing a draft evaluation report **6**  
Drafting and submission of the final draft report after incorporating input on the preliminary report and from the validation workshop **3**  
Validation workshop with IR Kenya and stakeholders **1**  
Incorporation of final report review comments and submission of final report to IR **3**  
**TOTAL** **35**

**9.0 Consultants Qualifications, Skills and Experience**  
The Consultant/s will possess the following minimum skills.  
• A minimum master’s degree in social sciences or a relevant field  
• At least 6 years’ experience undertaking evaluations and/or assessments for Food security, livelihoods, WASH, Education and integrated projects  
• Must have led at least two to three similar/assignments in the past 3 years  
• Proven skills in research, monitoring and evaluation  
• Proven experience in conducting qualitative, quantitative and mixed methods evaluation studies  
• Computer proficiency with good knowledge of MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and SPSS is desirable  
• Experience in undertaking evaluations in ASAL areas will be an added advantage  
• Excellent analytical and report writing skills  
• Excellent written and spoken English  
• Excellent time management skills  
• Ability to work well both independently and in a team  
• Excellent conflict-sensitive approaches and able to work in highly sensitive environments  
**10.0 ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS**  
The below ethical considerations will be adhered to during the evaluation survey:  
• IRW recognizes the personal dignity and rights of children and vulnerable adults, towards whom it has a special responsibility and duty of care and respect. The consultant is expected to adhere to the IRW Safeguarding policy and sign as an appendix to their contract of engagement and agree to conduct themselves by the provisions of these documents.  
• The evaluation will be conducted by an independent and impartial external consultant, assisted by the IR Kenya MEAL Teams.  
• Quantitative data will be obtained from a randomly selected representative population sample.  
• Assert that their participation in the survey will be voluntary, and they are aware that they can opt out at any time. (Note that participants may leave or refuse to answer any question at any time, and that this will not affect their standing with the organization.)  
• Anonymity, confidentiality and safeguarding of survey data will be guaranteed.  
• There will be no risks and benefits for individual participants  
• The culture, norms and traditions of study populations will be respected.  
• Consent will be sought before commencing data gathering  
• Views and opinions of the different survey subjects will be respected.  
• For interviews with children, there will be an informed consent process to ensure that all children, their parents/guardians and vulnerable adults are fully aware of all aspects of the evaluation process and voluntarily provide their consent to take part. All caregivers/guardians will be asked to provide informed consent for children’s participation in the study, in line with UNCRC’s recognition of children’s evolving capacities and a parent/guardian’s responsibility to ensure a child’s well-being and safety.  
• All the respondents’ data will be kept confidential and shared only with the consent of IR Kenya  
**11.0 Product rights and ownership**
