fields.title: PRF33834 Request for Proposals to Conduct Baseline Evaluation Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County(Phase II)
fields.body:
[https://kenyaredcross-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/tenders_redcross_or_ke/IQADcP_o5VapSLdp7-4uz8sKAeF9zakl_iM0GTydw1Ty7YM?e=BeQ06q](https://kenyaredcross-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/tenders_redcross_or_ke/IQADcP_o5VapSLdp7-4uz8sKAeF9zakl_iM0GTydw1Ty7YM?e=BeQ06q)

**Request for Proposals to Conduct**

**Baseline Evaluation**

**Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County (Phase II)**

**Document Release Date: 14/10/2026**

**Last Date for Receipt of Proposals: 28/10/2026**

**Time: 11:00 HRS**

**Tender Number: PRF33834**

**Submission Method: email to tenders@redcross.or.ke**

**Tender Opening Venue and Time: Virtually via Microsoft Teams at 1200hrs**

1. **Summary of the baseline survey**
    1. **Purpose**:

The baseline evaluation aims to establish the benchmark statistics for the project “Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County” (Phase II), a new phase of the Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS)/CBM Global “Promoting Inclusive Climate Change Resilience in Bungoma County” project (Phase I). It will document the current situation of target communities, including persons with disabilities, women, youth and other marginalized groups, against the Phase II results framework, validate the relevance and measurability of the log frame indicators and targets, and provide a robust reference point against which the project's future mid-term review and end-term evaluation will measure change.

**Partners**

CBM Global Disability Inclusion (CBM Global), Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS), Disability Empowerment Network (DEN), National Government, Bungoma County Government and relevant departments (Directorate of Climate Change, Ministry of Water, Tourism, Environment and Natural Resources, Ministry of Youth, Gender and Social Development, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Labor and Social Protection, National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD), Association for Persons with Disability Kenya (APDK), Kenya Meteorological Department, Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs)).

**Duration**

35 days

**Estimated Dates**

5/11/2026 – 9/12/2026

**Geographical Location**

Bungoma County, Kenya - focusing on Tongaren, Bumula and Webuye East sub-counties

**Target Population**

Persons with disabilities (men, women, boys and girls), women- and youth-headed households, older persons, indigenous and other marginalized community members, Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), Ward Climate Committees, Village Savings and Loan Association (VSLA)/self-help groups, County and Sub-County Government departments (climate change, disaster management, health, social protection), and Kenya Red Cross Society/DEN staff and volunteers.

**Deliverables**

Inception report and tools, cleaned datasets and codebook, draft and final baseline report, PowerPoint presentation, dissemination/validation workshop, and an easy-read version of the report.

**Methodology**

Mixed methods - quantitative and qualitative, disability- and gender-inclusive data collection approaches.

**Evaluation Management Team**

KRCS MEA&L team, KRCS Project representatives, and CBM Global representative(s).

1. **Background Information**

Climate Change is a threat to the development of the global economy and the greatest impediment to the achievement of sustainable development goals. Current global weather extremes affect millions of people, resulting in food and water insecurity in addition to affecting agricultural productivity. In Kenya, Climate Change has resulted in extreme weather events that have led to loss of lives, reduced agricultural productivity, displacement of populations, and destruction of infrastructure, among other adverse impacts. Bungoma County has also not been spared, with increased cases of flooding, landslides, and drought resulting in displacement of people, damage to infrastructure and low agricultural yields.

According to the 2019 Kenya census report, an estimated 40,186 persons with disabilities live in Bungoma County, representing 2.4% of the population. This population continues to face disproportionate risks due to structural barriers such as limited access to climate information, restricted mobility, limited access to services, and exclusion from planning and decision-making spaces at community and county levels. Barriers to their full participation in society prior to disasters and other emergencies tend to be exacerbated by climate-related hazards, and failure to consult persons with disabilities and their representative organizations in the development of plans to respond to emergencies increases their risks and vulnerabilities.

With support from and in partnership with CBM Global, Kenya Red Cross Society implemented a 3-year project dubbed “Promoting Inclusive Climate Change Resilience in Bungoma County” (Phase I, 2023-2025) in Cheptais, Kopsiro and Bungoma South (Kanduyi) sub-counties. Phase I demonstrated the feasibility and value of disability-inclusive climate action: it empowered more than 800 persons with disabilities to participate in climate resilience processes and reached over 20,000 community members through early warning dissemination, climate-smart livelihood activities, and community-led advocacy.

The Phase I end of project findings informed the design of Phase II, reflecting the learnings the results and the current needs. Building on the achievements, lessons and gaps identified under Phase I, KRCS and CBM Global have designed a new phase - “Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County” (Phase II, 1st July 2026 - 31st December 2028) - implemented by KRCS as lead implementing partner in partnership with the Disability Empowerment Network (DEN) as the primary sub-partner. The project will be implemented in Tongaren, Bumula and Webuye east sub-counties. Phase II adopts a rights-based, gender-responsive, disability-inclusive, and community-led approach that tackles the root causes of vulnerability while enhancing adaptive capacities. It combines: strengthened Inclusive Early Warning and Early Action (EWEA) systems using multiple, accessible communication channels for different disability groups; climate-smart livelihood interventions targeting women, youth, and persons with disabilities, including underrepresented and indigenous communities; capacity building of county institutions and community structures to institutionalize inclusive climate governance; and integration of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) to address the emotional and social impacts of climate-related stressors.

As the project design form notes that a baseline assessment is planned within the first quarter of project implementation, this baseline survey is required to establish reliable starting values for the Phase II log frame indicators, sharpen the theory of change, and inform the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEA&L) plan to be finalized within three months of project commencement.

1. **Project Objectives**

Overall Project Goal: To reduce the impacts of climate-related risks for communities by strengthening their capacity for preparedness, early action, and inclusive disaster risk management, while ensuring full participation and protection of persons with disabilities and other at-risk groups.

- Specific Objective 1: To strengthen the ability of at-risk communities to apply inclusive, climate-adaptive approaches and engage in advocacy mechanisms that enhance their participation and resilience to climate-related shocks.
- Specific Objective 2: To improve adaptive livelihoods, access to services, and social protection for persons with disabilities and at-risk households.
- Specific Objective 3: To strengthen evidence generation, advocacy and learning for inclusive climate action.

1. **Key Project Stakeholders**

The project is implemented in close coordination with the National and Bungoma County Governments and their departments, including the Directorate of Climate Change, the Ministry of Water, Tourism, Environment and Natural Resources, the Ministry of Youth, Gender and Social Development, the Ministry of Health (rehabilitation and physiotherapy departments), the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection, the National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD), the Kenya Meteorological Department, and the Association for Persons with Disability Kenya (APDK).

Key implementing partners are Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS), as lead implementing partner, and the Disability Empowerment Network (DEN), as primary sub-partner. The project also works with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), Ward Climate Committees, women-led organizations, grassroots community structures, VSLA/self-help groups, and National Government Administrative Officers. At the regional/global level, the project engages with the Early Warnings for All (EW4ALL) pillar leads (UNDRR, NDOC, WMO, ITU, CA, IFRC, KRCS).

1. **Baseline survey Purpose & Scope**
    1. **Purpose.**

The baseline survey aims to establish the current status of the target population and systems against each Phase II log frame indicator, ahead of project implementation. It will provide a credible evidence base against which project progress and impact will be measured at mid-term and end-term.

The baseline survey will establish the pre-intervention values for the Phase II log frame indicators in Tongaren, Webuye East and Bumula sub-counties. These values form the benchmark against which change will be measured at mid-term and end-term. The survey will also confirm that the indicators, targets and monitoring arrangements are realistic and measurable, so that the project can track and demonstrate its results from the start.

1. To establish baseline values for key project outcome and output indicators, including climate-related risks, community adaptive capacity and existing resilience practices across the three sub-counties.
2. To assess community perceptions and experiences of participation, disability inclusion, feedback, accountability and safeguarding mechanisms, and identify key gaps.
3. To identify priority project risks, assumptions and monitoring requirements that may affect implementation and achievement of results.
4. To provide practical recommendations to refine programme targeting, implementation, monitoring and learning.
5. **Key Questions**

The consultant will develop key questions to enable the baseline survey to generate the information needed on the project's starting context and indicators. The following are proposed key questions; the consultant may suggest changes/additional questions at the inception stage:

**Baseline values and indicators**

- What are the baseline values for each Phase II log frame indicator?
- Are the current indicators and targets realistic, measurable, and appropriately disaggregated (sex, age, disability, geography)?
- What data sources and collection methods are most appropriate for tracking each indicator going forward?

**Context and needs analysis**

- What is the current level of climate risk awareness, preparedness, and early warning access among target communities, disaggregated by gender and disability?
- What livelihood strategies do households, including persons with disabilities, currently use, and how climate-adaptive are they?
- What is the current status of VSLA/self-help groups, microenterprises, and access to rehabilitation and assistive devices in the target areas?
- What is the level of functioning of Ward Climate Committees, DRM coordination platforms, and OPD engagement in county governance processes?

**Capacity assessment**

- What is the current institutional and technical capacity of KRCS, DEN, OPDs, and county departments to deliver and monitor a disability-inclusive climate resilience project?
- Key MEA&L capacity gaps within DEN that require strengthening to enable DEN to meaningfully support MEA&L functions within the project.

**Community Engagement, Accountability and Safeguarding**

- What complaints and feedback mechanisms currently exist in the target communities, and how accessible are they to persons with disabilities?
- What safeguarding risks (including GBV, exploitation, and exclusion of persons with intellectual or psychosocial disabilities) are present in the target context, and what systems currently exist to mitigate them?
- To what extent are community members, including persons with disabilities and women, currently involved in decision-making processes relevant to climate resilience?

**Gender and Disability Inclusion**

- What specific barriers do women, men, persons with disabilities (by type), youth and older persons currently face in accessing climate information, livelihoods, and services?
- How are gender relations, decision-making power, and leadership currently distributed within target communities and OPDs?

**Risks and Assumptions**

- Are the key assumptions in the log frame (e.g. continued institutional commitment, market functionality, community adoption of livelihood diversification) currently valid in the project context?
- What additional risks (climate, security, political, or operational) should be considered in the project's risk register?

1. **Survey Methodology**

The consultant will be expected to propose the most appropriate study design, sampling methods, sample size, and data collection and analysis approaches for the baseline survey. These should be clearly outlined in the bidding document/proposal and will be further discussed with the assessment management team if the firm qualifies for the oral stage. The firm should identify and justify the target respondents or data sources that can effectively address the log frame indicators. The proposed methodology should incorporate triangulation of findings and ensure an adequate, representative sample of the target beneficiaries, with clearly defined sampling procedures, disaggregated by sex, age, and disability status (using, for example, the Washington Group Questions).

All log frame indicators should be given operational definitions in the bid submission. A detailed data analysis plan should also be included, indicating how each indicator will be analyzed, and how baseline values will be presented and structured to allow direct comparison at mid-term and end-term.

Additional documents that can be used during the baseline survey include the following, in additional to any other relevant documents/literature to inform the survey process:

- Phase I End-Term Evaluation report and Phase I project reports.
- Phase II project design form, theory of change, and log frame.
- Phase II project risk register and safeguarding risk assessment.
- Existing needs assessments and contextual analyses for Bungoma County.
- Documents, policies and frameworks by partners, county and national government (e.g. Bungoma County Integrated Development Plan (CIDP) 2023-2027, Kenya Climate Change Act 2016, National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) 2023-2027, Disability Inclusion Policy).

The project's Overall Objective, Specific Objectives and Results-level indicators are shown in the table below:

**Hierarchy of Objectives**

**Objectively Verifiable Indicators (OVI)**

**Overall Objective (Impact):**

**Strengthened disability-inclusive, gender-responsive, and community-led climate resilience systems in Bungoma County.**

**Specific Objective 1 (Outcome):**

**Communities at risk of climate shocks in Bungoma County apply inclusive coping, early warning, and advocacy mechanisms that reduce vulnerability and strengthen resilience.**

% of supported communities implementing inclusive early warning and coping mechanisms. (Survey reports)

% of persons with disability, women, and marginalized persons accessing and responding to early warning information. (Surveys)

% of supported households reporting diversified and climate-adaptive livelihoods (Surveys)

**Result 1.1 (output):**

**Coping mechanisms of communities at risk of climate shocks are strengthened.**

Number of Ward Climate Committees applying disability- and gender-inclusive planning.

Number of at risk households supported with inclusive climate-adaptive livelihoods.

Number of strengthened VSLA groups which are functional.

**Result 1.2 (output):**

**Participatory, community-led Early Warning Early Action (EWEA) systems accessible to all (including persons with disabilities) are strengthened.**

% of persons with disabilities reporting access to timely and understandable early warning information.

Number of functional DRM coordination platforms at ward, sub-county and county levels. Baseline (Phase I):

Number of persons accessing rehabilitation, assistive devices and referral services.

**Result 1.3 (output):**

**Strengthened gender, age and disability-inclusive climate governance through OPD-led advocacy.**

Number of OPDs actively participating in county climate and DRM governance processes.

Number of OPD-led advocacy initiatives on inclusive climate action.

Number of county plans, policies or processes influenced by OPD advocacy.

**Result 1.4 (Output**

**Project accountability, safeguarding, monitoring and learning systems strengthened.**

Number of joint monitoring visits conducted.

% of beneficiaries reporting satisfaction with project services.

Number of learning and advocacy products developed.

**Specific Objective 2 (Outcome):**

**Improve adaptive livelihoods, access to services, and social protection for persons with disabilities and at-risk households.**

% of targeted households demonstrating improved income and livelihood diversification.

% of people (persons with disabilities/women) reporting increased access to social protection or adaptive livelihood schemes.

Number of persons with disabilities, women, and marginalized persons engaged in climate-smart livelihood initiatives.

**Result 2.1 (Output):**

**Persons with disabilities, women and other marginalized groups have improved access to adaptive, climate-smart livelihoods and initiatives.**

Number of livelihood interventions designed with inclusive adaptation measures.

Average household income of participants.

Number of persons with disabilities, women, and marginalized persons participating in climate-smart livelihood projects.

**Result 2.2 (Output):**

**Rehabilitation and assistive technology services are scaled up and linked to livelihood and resilience initiatives.**

Number of livelihood initiatives integrating access to rehabilitation or assistive services.

Number of beneficiaries accessing assistive devices to support participation in livelihood activities.

Number of partnerships established between service providers and livelihood programmes.

**Result 2.3 (Output):**

**Households demonstrate improved economic resilience through inclusive VSLA and microenterprise support.**

% of VSLA members reporting increased savings and business income.

Number of inclusive VSLA groups formed/strengthened with persons with disability and gender representation.

Number of microenterprises initiated or scaled by persons with disability and women.

**Result 2.4: Output**

**Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) and GBV protection integrated into livelihood and community resilience programming.**

% of persons with disabilities and women reporting access to psychosocial and protection services.

Number of referral linkages established between livelihood and GBV/MHPSS service providers.

Number of persons referred through the linkages.

**Specific Objective 3 (Outcome):**

**Strengthen evidence generation, advocacy and learning for inclusive climate action.**

Number of inclusive advocacy initiatives or policy dialogues influenced by project evidence.

Number of policy briefs, learning papers, or case studies produced and disseminated.

**Result 3.1 (Short-term Outcome):**

**Data on disability inclusion, gender, and climate impact systematically collected and shared.**

Number of inclusive data collection tools developed and used.

Number of county climate reports that include disaggregated data (sex, age, disability).

Number of data-sharing platforms or repositories established and maintained.

**Result 3.2 (Short-term Outcome):**

**Policy briefs, learning papers, and evidence disseminated to inform county, national, and regional platforms.**

Number of policy briefs, case studies, and learning papers developed and disseminated.

Number of forums/events where inclusive climate data/evidence is presented. Baseline (Phase I): 1.

Number of instances where evidence informs policy decisions or planning processes.

**Result 3.3 (Short-term Outcome):**

**OPDs and county actors demonstrate improved capacity for inclusive advocacy and monitoring.**

Number of OPDs applying advocacy and monitoring skills in county planning processes.

Number of joint advocacy initiatives led by OPDs and county actors on inclusive climate resilience.

Number of OPD and county actors reporting improved capacities.

1. **Quality & Ethical Standards**

The consultant shall take all reasonable steps to ensure that the survey is designed and conducted to respect and protect the rights and welfare of the people and communities involved and to ensure that the assessment is technically accurate and reliable, is conducted in a transparent and impartial manner, and contributes to organizational learning and accountability. Therefore, the survey team shall be required to adhere to the assessment standards and applicable practices as recommended by the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

- **Utility:** Assessments must be useful and used.
- **Feasibility:** Assessments must be realistic, diplomatic, and managed in a sensible, cost-effective manner.
- **Ethics & Legality:** Assessments must be conducted ethically and legally, with regard for the welfare of those involved in and affected by the assessment.
- **Impartiality & Independence:** Assessments should be impartial, providing a comprehensive and unbiased assessment that considers the views of all stakeholders.
- **Transparency:** Assessment activities should reflect an attitude of openness and transparency.
- **Accuracy:** Assessments should be technically accurate, providing sufficient information about the data collection, analysis, and interpretation methods so that its worth or merit can be determined.
- **Participation:** Stakeholders should be consulted and meaningfully involved in the assessment process when feasible and appropriate.
- **Collaboration:** Collaboration between key operating partners in the assessment process improves the legitimacy and utility of the assessment.
- **Inclusion:** The assessment must include clear steps to ensure meaningful engagement and participation of all sections of the community, including persons with disabilities and women.

It is also expected that the assessment will respect the seven Fundamental Principles of the Red Cross and Red Crescent: 1) humanity, 2) impartiality, 3) neutrality, 4) independence, 5) voluntary service, 6) unity and 7) universality.

1. **Qualifications and Experience for Consultants**

The lead consultant must possess the following qualifications:

1. A minimum of a master’s degree in Public Health/climate change and adaptation/environmental science and Environmental studies/disaster risk management & disaster preparedness/sustainable development/development studies/project planning and management/Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) or Applied Researchor related field.
2. A minimum of 5 years’ extensive experience in carrying out comprehensive baselines or similar assignments.
3. Good understanding of climate change and climate-related risks, with demonstrated expertise in mainstreaming gender equality, disability inclusion, and age considerations among vulnerable populations in Kenya.
4. Proven experience in participatory and results-based M&E knowledge and practical experience in quantitative and qualitative research methods.
5. Must have led at least five participatory assessments. Experience of conducting evaluations, monitoring and assessment work in the target or similar communities (preferred).
6. High level of professionalism and an ability to work independently and in high-pressure situations under tight deadlines.

fields.title: Monitoring and Evaluation Advisor
fields.body:
## About the Role

All Hands and Hearts is seeking an experienced Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Advisor to build and lead the monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning systems for its humanitarian response in Gaza. Operating in a fast-changing environment with constrained access, AHAH needs reliable, timely evidence on what is reaching communities, what is working, and where programs must adapt. The successful candidate will focus primarily on nutrition Monitoring and Evaluation, ensure quality data collection and reporting to leadership and donors, and put in place mechanisms that let affected communities give feedback and hold the organization accountable.

## Key Responsibilities

- **M&E Systems and Frameworks:** Design and roll out AHAH's M&E framework for Gaza nutrition program, including results frameworks, data collection and analysis, indicator reference sheets and performance monitoring plans aligned with donor requirements and cluster standards.
- **Distribution and Commodity Monitoring:** Establish post-distribution monitoring, commodity tracking and verification processes to confirm that AHAH assistance reaches intended civilian beneficiaries, and flag diversion or access risks to leadership.
- **Data Collection and Management:** Develop data collection tools and lead the use of mobile data platforms; ensure data quality, security, beneficiary data protection and safe storage.
- **Assessments and Evaluations:** Lead or support needs assessments, baseline and endline surveys, and periodic program reviews; manage external evaluations where required.
- **Reporting and Learning:** Produce timely, accurate reports and dashboards for AHAH leadership and donors; document lessons learned and use findings to guide program adaptation.
- **Coordination:** Represent AHAH in inter-agency information management and assessment working groups; contribute data to cluster reporting, as appropriate.
- **Capacity Building:** Train and mentor field staff, on M&E methods, data collection and ethical data practices.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Contribute M&E plans, indicators and budgets to proposals for institutional and private donors.

## Qualifications & Experience

- Master's degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Public Health, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Minimum 8–10 years of M&E experience, including at least 5 years in humanitarian or emergency settings.
- Demonstrated expertise in designing M&E systems, quantitative and qualitative methods, and donor reporting.
- Proficiency with mobile data collection platforms and data analysis tools
- Excellent analytical, communication and report-writing skills.
- Language requirements: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).
- Candidates must be willing to undergo a thorough background and security check prior to a final offer. Must demonstrate commitment to neutrality and community service.

## Salary

This is an 18-month, fixed-term contract/consultancy with compensation that will be competitive based on experience and location.

fields.title: National MEAL Coordinator
fields.body:
## Background

The CORE Group Partners Project (CGPP) is a multi-country, multi-partner initiative that provides on-the-ground technical assistance and guidance to support host country efforts to strengthen immunization systems, disease surveillance, and essential community-based health services. Globally, CGPP works across five technical areas (polio, maternal and child health, nutrition, malaria, and global health security) through existing networks of international and local NGOs operating in hard-to-reach areas with low immunization coverage. At the country level, a Secretariat coordinates the work of CGPP partner organizations in a manner that complements the efforts of all implementing partners. In Indonesia, CGPP supports national health strategies by strengthening routine immunization and polio eradication efforts while promoting maternal and child health through integrated community-based interventions.

CGPP works with the Government of Indonesia to improve maternal and child health (MCH) outcomes and strengthen routine immunization and polio eradication in selected districts of Papua and East Java and other CGPP-supported areas.

The CGPP Indonesia Secretariat, led by the Secretariat Director based in Jakarta, coordinates with the Ministry of Health (MOH) and other ministries, US Department of State (US DOS) Foreign Assistance team, UNICEF, STRIDES (FHI 360), other Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) partners, and Wahana Visi / World Vision Indonesia. The Director regularly briefs these stakeholders on project performance. Those briefings depend on project data that is complete, validated, and consistent with national MOH indicators and US DOS reporting requirements.

## Purpose of the Consultancy

CGPP Indonesia will engage a National MEAL Coordinator as a full-time consultant to make every number, report, and presentation that the Secretariat Director takes to the MOH and the US DOS accurate, consistent, and on time.

The National MEAL Coordinator will provide oversight support to CGPP Indonesia to ensure quality data and reporting. Working under the guidance of the CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director, the consultant will:

1. Ensure CGPP project data is complete, accurate, timely and consistent with national MOH guidelines and indicator definitions and with US DOS Foreign Assistance reporting guidelines.
2. Ensure the quality of all CGPP Indonesia reports, data summaries, and briefings before submission.
3. Prepare and quality-check the presentations and briefing materials the Secretariat Director uses with MOH, US DOS, GPEI partners, and other forums.
4. Strengthen MEAL systems and capacity across the Secretariat and partner teams so that data is used for decisions and learning.

## Scope of Work and Key Responsibilities

### 1. Data quality and alignment with MOH and US DOS guidelines

- Review the CGPP Indonesia MEAL framework, indicator reference sheets, and data collection tools; align to CGPP Global MEAL Framework, indicator definitions, disaggregation, and reporting periods with MOH national standards (immunization, MCH, and surveillance systems) and with US DOS Foreign Assistance reporting requirements.
- Map source of the CGPP data (community, health facility, district, and partner sources) and document data flows, responsibilities, and reporting timelines.
- Establish and run a routine data quality assurance system: monthly validation checks, periodic data quality assessments (DQAs), and spot checks during field visits.
- Reconcile CGPP-reported results with MOH district and provincial data; flag and resolve discrepancies with field teams and partners before results are reported.
- Maintain a single, version-controlled master dataset and indicator tracking table as the official source for all CGPP Indonesia figures.

### 2. Quality of reports

- Review all CGPP Indonesia reports before submission (monthly updates, quarterly and semi-annual reports, annual reports, and ad hoc donor requests) for data accuracy, internal consistency, correct use of indicators, and clear analysis.
- Validate monthly data updates, performance indicators, and partner-reported results, as required by the Secretariat Director.
- Develop standard reporting templates and a reporting calendar with internal deadlines that allow time for review.
- Write the results and data analysis sections of reports, including progress against targets and explanations of variance.

### 3. Presentations and briefings for the Secretariat Director

- Prepare data-driven presentations, briefing notes, fact sheets, and talking points for the Director's meetings with MOH, US DOS, GPEI partners, UNICEF, STRIDES, and other coordination forums.
- Ensure every figure in these materials matches the master dataset and the latest submitted report.
- Produce clear charts, maps, and dashboards that show progress, gaps, and priority actions.
- Attend key meetings with the Director when requested, capture data-related questions and action points, and follow up.
- As per guidance of the CGPP Indonesia Director, represent CGPP Indonesia in national-level platforms.

### 4. Monitoring, evaluation, and learning

- Support the design and management of planned CGPP assessments, surveys, and evaluations, including terms of reference, tools, data analysis, and reports.
- Lead regular data review and reflection meetings with the Secretariat and provincial teams to turn findings into program adjustments.
- Document lessons learned, success stories, and good practices for internal learning and external sharing.

### 5. MEAL systems and capacity strengthening

- Work with the CGPP National Program Manager and MEAL team to harmonize workflows and maintain common MEAL standards across all partners.
- Train and mentor national and provincial staff on indicators, data collection, data quality, and data use.
- Recommend practical improvements to digital data tools and dashboards, in line with MOH systems.

### 6. Accountability

- Support community feedback and accountability mechanisms so community concerns are recorded, analyzed, and reported to decision-makers.
- Ensure data protection, confidentiality, and ethical standards in all data collection and storage.

## Reporting and Working Relationships

- **Reports to:** CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director, who sets priorities, approves deliverables, and certifies payment.
- **Technical guidance:** CGPP Global Secretariat MEAL team and Senior Technical Advisor, for global indicator and reporting standards and program quality.
- **Internal:** CGPP National Program Manager, CGPP Indonesia MEAL team, Provincial Team Leaders, Wahana Visi / World Vision Indonesia program and MEAL staff, and finance and grants teams.
- **External:** MOH (national, provincial, and district health offices), US DOS Foreign Assistance team, UNICEF, STRIDES (FHI 360), and other GPEI partners, for data-related coordination as delegated by the Director.
- **Supervisory responsibility:** None. As a consultant, the MEAL Coordinator provides technical guidance and mentoring but does not supervise staff.

## Qualifications and Experience

### Required

- Master's degree in public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, demography, or a related field.
- At least 8 years of experience in monitoring and evaluation of public health programs, including at least 3 years leading MEAL for donor-funded projects.
- Hands-on knowledge of Indonesian MOH health information systems and indicators, especially immunization, MCH, and surveillance.
- Proven experience in data quality assessment, data validation, and reconciliation with government data.
- Experience preparing donor reports and presentations for senior government and donor audiences; US Government reporting experience strongly preferred.
- Strong skills in Excel and at least one statistical or visualization tool (e.g. Stata, SPSS, R, Power BI, or Tableau); experience with DHIS2, KoboToolbox, or ODK is an advantage.

### Preferred

- Experience with polio eradication, routine immunization, and MCH or GPEI partner programs.
- Work experience in Indonesia.
- Experience designing and managing surveys and evaluations.

### Skills and Abilities

- Close attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
- Ability to turn complex data into clear messages, charts and briefings.
- Ability to work to tight deadlines and manage several reports at once.
- Strong interpersonal skills to work with government, donors and partners.

### Languages

- **English**: Professional proficiency required, with ability to communicate effectively in writing and speech and with excellent report-writing in English.
- **Bahasa Indonesia**: Professional proficiency required in speaking, reading, and writing.

### Travel

- Must be willing to travel approximately 25-35% of the time.

## Terms

- **Contract:** Full-time consultancy with CORE Group, Inc., November 1, 2026 – August 31, 2027, with possible extension based on performance and funding.
- **Payment:** Monthly fee, paid on submission and approval of the monthly activity report, timesheet, and deliverables due that month. Travel costs are covered per CORE Group, Inc. policy.
- **Data ownership:** All data, reports, and materials produced belong to CGPP and may not be shared without the Secretariat Director's written approval.
- **Safeguarding:** The consultant must comply with CORE Group codes of conduct, including safeguarding and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse.

## Disclaimer

- This scope of work is not an exhaustive list of the skills, effort, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position.

**CONSULTANCY TITLE:** Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Consultant

**CATEGORY**: Professional Consultant

**LOCATION:** Nairobi, Kenya, Remote

**DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT:** 30 days from October 26, 2026, to June 30, 2027.

**EMAIL SUBJECT LINE**: *Consultancy – Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Expert*

**Background**

Population Council- Kenya (PC Kenya), a non-profit organization registered in Kenya, is leading an inter-regional consortium of Function-Oriented Impact Partner Organizations (IPOs) that comprises ThinkPlace Kenya, Le Barometre, and the Centre for the Study of the Economies of Africa (CSEA) (the IPO). The IPO supports Mastercard Foundation’s Impact Strategy by conducting impact measurement and evaluation activities, in addition to supporting program design and learnings across the Foundation’s program platforms, namely, the Pan-Africa Program (PANA), Scholars, Secondary Education and Transition (SET), Higher Education Collaboratives and Strategic Initiatives (HECSI), and Strategic Partnerships and Innovations (SP&I). The geographic scope of programs supported by the Foundation cuts across 35 countries in Africa. The IPO supports the Foundation and its partners through:

1. **Impact Technical Delivery**, which includes supporting robust monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) processes that entail assessing the progress of programs in advancing the Foundation's charitable goals of financial inclusion and youth education, as well as achieving set targets across the various programmatic platforms.
2. **Program Support**, that entails supporting the development of strategies tailored to the unique needs of the Foundation’s partners and program participants through extensive evidence reviews, needs assessments, and participatory design methods to ensure interventions are designed to achieve impact in line with specific platform strategies and the Foundation’s charitable purpose.
3. **Cross-cutting Support**, which entails supporting field building and communications activities through training and knowledge sharing and reflection to promote adoption of best practices.

The IPO provides technical support to the Foundation and its implementing partners on strategies that strengthen theories of change (ToCs) and monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) frameworks, including supporting refinement of ToCs, MEL key performance indicators (KPIs) and learning questions, in addition to tracking partners’ MEL capabilities, and providing technical support to strengthen those capabilities.

**Scope of Work**

PC Kenya is seeking the services of a professional consultant to support the IPO, the Foundation and its implementing partners. The purpose of the assignment is to support the IPO to establish and deliver a structured MEL accompaniment programme for Foundation implementing partners. The programme will strengthen partner-level MEL infrastructure, governance, systems, processes, capabilities and use of evidence for decisions and reporting. Support will be tailored to documented partner needs and will cover theories of change, MEL plans, indicators, learning questions, data architecture, participant-level records, data quality, data governance, analysis, reporting, learning and adaptive management. The consultant will work with the IPO to perform the following tasks:

**Workstream 1: Inception, partner universe and prioritisation**

1. Review the Platform framework, partner portfolio, IPO plans, relevant MEL guidance, Shared Measures 2.0 requirements, Comprehensive Approach to Reviews and Evaluation (CARE), Program Outcomes Assessment/ Data Quality Assessment (POA/DQA) findings, Fluxx/Daraja reporting requirements and existing partner MEL documentation.
2. Confirm the partners and programmes covered by the assignment.
3. Establish a partner-level MEL support register and prioritisation methodology.
4. Prepare a detailed workplan showing partners, needs, activities, dates, responsibilities, level of effort, intended results and dependencies.

**Workstream 2: Partner MEL capability and system diagnostics**

1. Assess the MEL capability, infrastructure and operational readiness of agreed partners.
2. Review partner ToCs, results chains, MEL plans, indicators, targets, learning questions, data tools, participant-management systems, reporting arrangements and evidence-use practices.
3. Integrate relevant DQA, POA and review findings into each diagnostic.
4. Produce an agreed improvement plan for each partner or coherent partner cluster.

**Workstream 3: MEL framework and infrastructure strengthening**

1. Support partners to refine and operationalise ToCs, MEL plans, indicators, learning questions, tools, protocols and reporting calendars.
2. Strengthen data architecture, participant-level records, data dictionaries, indicator reference sheets, collection processes, storage, access controls, cleaning, validation and documentation.
3. Clarify data flows and accountabilities between lead partners, sub-partners, collaboratives, IPOs, programme teams and the Foundation.
4. Support partners to establish practical DQA and data-correction routines.

**Workstream 4: Measurement alignment**

1. Support operational alignment with Shared Measures 2.0 and applicable Work-Enabling Outreach (WEO), Youth-in-Work (YiW), transitions, inclusion, institutional strengthening and systems-change measures.
2. Confirm indicator applicability, targets, disaggregation, sources, frequency, aggregation, attribution and reporting responsibilities.
3. Identify and address gaps between partner records, programme designs and Fluxx/Daraja reporting requirements.
4. Support credible treatment of collaborative contributions and risks of double counting.

**Workstream 5: Learning and adaptive management**

1. Support partners to strengthen learning agendas and routine evidence reflection.
2. Facilitate or support partner-specific working sessions, coaching and communities of practice.
3. Establish decision logs linking evidence and insights to adaptations.

fields.body:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/200**
- **Position Title**: Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert - CDR
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 3 months (without exceeding 16 working days per month).
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 14 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 21 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JFJvvMi0X1CMbBMR4IhA-Zv5eASVx6wv/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JFJvvMi0X1CMbBMR4IhA-Zv5eASVx6wv/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), operating under the Council of Ministers, plays a central role in Lebanon’s development planning, infrastructure projects, coordination with development partners, and reconstruction efforts. The prolonged crisis has placed pressure on its human resources and operational capacity, highlighting the need to strengthen its institutional arrangements, organizational structure, and business processes to respond effectively to evolving priorities.

In response, a comprehensive Functional and Business Process Review of CDR was undertaken to assess the institution’s existing functions, organizational arrangements, business processes, governance mechanisms, and staffing requirements, and to identify measures to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. The findings and recommendations of the review have been consolidated in an implementation roadmap. The roadmap distinguishes between measures that can be implemented within the existing legal and regulatory framework, referred to as the Interim Arrangements, and reforms that require amendments to Decree No. 10941 of 2003 and Decree No. 10942 of 2003, referred to as the Target Roadmap. The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

The successful implementation of CDR’s digital transformation requires the establishment of a clear governance and implementation foundation before major technology investments and platform deployments can proceed. This includes defining ownership and decision-making arrangements, validating the target structure and functions of the Information Technology Department, establishing an enterprise architecture and data governance framework, and ensuring that core business processes are appropriately re-baselined to reflect the future operating model. It also requires a clear understanding of CDR’s existing technology, systems, data, infrastructure, and security environment, together with a structured approach to prioritizing investments and addressing critical gaps.

Therefore, a set of foundational measures have been identified to be undertaken during Stage 1 of the Digital Transformation Roadmap. These measures are intended to establish the rules, governance arrangements, technical and organizational architecture, inventories, and implementation baseline required to guide subsequent phases of digital transformation. They include the establishment of programme governance arrangements, validation of the target IT Department structure and enterprise architecture, definition of data governance principles, risk-based re-baselining of core processes, and preparation of the inventories, procurement strategy, terms of reference, and multi-year budgets required to move from planning to implementation. Immediate actions have also been identified to strengthen CDR’s existing backup, recovery, and cybersecurity arrangements using available tools and resources, alongside urgent remediation measures that need to be initiated.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert to support CDR in delivering Stage 1 of the Digital Transformation Program. The Expert will establish the programme governance arrangements and implementation baseline, validate the target IT Department structure and enterprise architecture, define the foundations for data governance, and validate the priority use cases of the document management system and the shared workflow system. The Expert will also prepare the key inventories, procurement strategy, terms of reference, and multi-year budget requirements needed to enable subsequent digital investments and implementation.

Through this assignment, the Expert will support CDR in moving from the recommendations of the Functional and Business Process Review to a structured and implementable digital transformation programme, ensuring that the institutional, governance, process, technical, procurement, and financial foundations are in place before major digital platforms and systems proceed to implementation.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1. Program Governance and Mobilization**

- Within two weeks of mobilization, agree with CDR the process scope, the technical changes, the available working days and the resources required for this assignment, and prepare a work plan that schedules the remaining work with its owners, dependencies and costs.
- Support CDR in establishing the governance bodies of the Digital Transformation Program, comprising the ICT Steering Committee, the Data Governance Committee and the Technical Review Committee, and prepare their terms of reference, their decision rights and the responsibility matrix that assigns each decision to a named body. The terms of reference of the ICT Steering Committee cover its decisions, escalation arrangements, meeting frequency and progress reporting. Support CDR management in formally designating the interim ICT Transformation Lead and the business and technical owners of critical systems and services.
- Support the establishment of the Digital Transformation Program Office function, comprising the integrated roadmap, the dependency register, the risk register, the benefits plan, the procurement plan, the architecture decision log and the reporting calendar, and hand the instruments over in working order.
- Assist in validation of the target structure and staffing of the Information Technology Department against the functions the program requires, the existing staff and their workload, and coordinate the resulting job descriptions with the human resources workstream so that a single set of descriptions is produced. Prepare the responsibility matrix of the Department, identify staffing and skills gaps, and recommend interim assignments, training and specialist support. Formal appointments and organizational decisions remain with CDR.

**Workstream 2. Architecture and Data Governance**

- Develop and validate the enterprise architecture and the digital building blocks against the baseline covering the business, data, application, integration, technology and governance domains. Produce an updated high-level application and integration diagram, confirm the roles of JDE, the document management system, ArcGIS and the planned systems, and record the compatibility issues, dependencies and decisions required before procurement.
- Support in establishing the standing coordination arrangement with the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform and, where relevant, with the national digital acceleration program, with a designated focal point, a defined agenda covering hosting, interoperability, digital identity and electronic signature, and a reporting line to the ICT Steering Committee.
- Prepare the initial data governance principles, covering named business data owners, authoritative systems, shared project and contract identifiers, minimum metadata, access and classification, data quality, retention and controlled sharing. Submit the principles, with the validated enterprise architecture, to the ICT Steering Committee for endorsement.

**Workstream 3. Process Re-baselining and Technical Readiness**

- With the business service owners, review the process maps to identify the common requirements for the document management system and the shared workflow system. Validate representative use cases, bottlenecks, document types and control needs to the level required for the terms of reference. Validate the approval thresholds and segregation of duties for these use cases, and record unresolved decisions and required authorizations. Produce a prioritized catalogue of business flows for later implementation. Full process redesign and configuration follow in later stages.
- Prepare the system, application, asset and workload inventories, including hardware, software licenses, contracts and support arrangements, and record the baseline performance indicators, or the method for collecting them where data are not yet available, against which the benefits of the program are later measured. The inventories record quantities, condition, capacity, hosted workloads, owners, dependencies, support status and renewal dates. They also assess workstation upgrade readiness and the priority server, storage, backup, scanner and power-protection needs. The workload inventory of the hosts designated for retirement, prepared by the firm contracted for the server refresh, is incorporated rather than repeated.

**Workstream 4. Procurement and Funding Readiness**

- Prepare the phased procurement strategy. The strategy specifies the document management system and the shared workflow system during this assignment, establishes and accepts the platform in a later stage, and configures the priority business flows in successive releases. Identify the packages, dependencies, lead times and owners, and define separate deliverables and acceptance gates for the platform foundation and for each business-flow release.
- Prepare the technical specifications, quantities and supplier pricing schedule for the justified priority hardware, infrastructure and services. Compare reuse, support renewal, repair and replacement, and include capacity, compatibility, migration, warranty, support response, acceptance testing and staff handover requirements.
- Reconcile the installed software and its use with entitlements and contracts. Verify the current vendor lifecycle and upgrade terms for operating systems, productivity tools, server and database licenses, electronic mail, endpoint protection, backup, firewalls and core applications. Identify renewals, unused entitlements and license gaps, and prepare a costed renewal and upgrade schedule.
- Prepare the terms of reference for the document management system and the shared workflow system, assessing the modernization of the existing SharePoint environment against its replacement. Define document capture, metadata, search, versioning, retention, permissions and audit trails; reusable forms, routing, approvals, notifications and monitoring; configurable roles, approval rules and audit controls; integration with JDE and identity services; and migration, hosting, licensing, training and support. Specify the platform acceptance tests and the later releases of priority business flows. The requirements preserve CDR data ownership, editable documentation, interoperability, portability and exit rights, with brand-neutral specifications where feasible.
- Prepare the indicative multi-year budget for the three-year horizon of the roadmap, separating implementation costs from recurring costs, and covering operations, maintenance, staffing, training, security reviews, licensing, hosting, support, hardware refresh, integration maintenance and contingency, and confirm the institutional and budget owner of each system before procurement.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 16 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 16 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature, and to be completed by the 31st of January 2027.

Any continuation of the services beyond this period, including the second phase of support described in the Background, is subject to a separate contract or a formal amendment of this contract. Continuation depends on satisfactory performance under this contract, the continued requirement for the services and the availability of funds.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Digital Transformation, Information Management, Engineering, Business Administration, Public Administration or a related field. Specialized focus on enterprise architecture, information systems, digital transformation, data governance, cybersecurity, or ICT management is highly preferred.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) designing, managing, or implementing digital transformation and information management programmes, including ICT governance, enterprise architecture, systems integration, data governance, and business-process digitization; and (ii) providing strategic and technical advice on ICT infrastructure, cybersecurity, information systems, technology procurement, and digital transformation planning, preferably in public-sector or institutional environments.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

fields.title: AI and Digital Transformation Advisor
fields.body:
We are currently recruiting an **AI and Digital Transformation Advisor** to join our **Quality, Impact and Innovation Department**.

This is a **remote, 12-month position** open to candidates based in **the UK, or any Relief International country of operation within a +/- 4-hour difference from Central European Time (CET)**. The role has a global remit and works across departments and country programmes to help shape how Relief International adopts and benefits from artificial intelligence and digital transformation.

At Relief International, we are committed to building a representative, inclusive and authentic workplace. We strongly encourage applications from candidates from minoritized backgrounds and those who bring lived experience of the contexts in which we work.

This role is classified as requiring **standard pre-employment checks.**

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. Our team of more than 4,000 staff and local volunteers work across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, delivering Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience. We do this by working with local actors to develop safe, inclusive and evidence-based programming that is conflict-sensitive, climate-smart and responsive to community needs.

**About the Opportunity**

Artificial intelligence is transforming how organizations work, learn and make decisions. At Relief International, we see AI as an opportunity to strengthen humanitarian impact, improve efficiency, enhance knowledge sharing and support better decision-making across our global operations.

The AI and Digital Transformation Advisor will lead the development and implementation of Relief International's AI strategy, helping departments identify practical opportunities where AI and digital tools can create meaningful value. Rather than acting as a technical implementer, you will serve as a strategic advisor, facilitator and change leader, supporting teams to adopt AI responsibly, effectively and sustainably.

You will work closely with senior leaders, department heads, country directors and IT colleagues to develop an organizational roadmap for AI adoption, coordinate a portfolio of AI initiatives, strengthen staff capability and ensure that innovation remains aligned with organizational priorities, governance requirements and humanitarian principles.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is passionate about the practical application of AI and digital transformation and wants to help shape how a global humanitarian organization leverages emerging technologies to better serve vulnerable communities around the world.

**Your Responsibilities**

This role includes the following responsibilities.

- Lead the development and continuous evolution of Relief International's AI and digital transformation strategy, translating organizational priorities into a practical roadmap of initiatives and opportunities.
- Identify and prioritize opportunities where AI and digital tools can improve efficiency, effectiveness, quality, knowledge management and decision-making across departments and country programmes.
- Coordinate and oversee a portfolio of AI initiatives, ensuring clear objectives, ownership, milestones and measures of success while maintaining responsibility within individual departments.
- Support senior leaders and functional teams in developing business cases for AI adoption, tracking technology investments, licensing costs and demonstrating organizational value and return on investment.

- Work closely with IT and other stakeholders to ensure AI solutions align with cybersecurity, information security, data protection and governance requirements.
- Promote the responsible use of AI, including appropriate human oversight, data privacy, transparency, accuracy and awareness of bias and limitations.
- Lead initiatives that strengthen organizational learning and knowledge management, including the use of AI-enabled approaches to make institutional knowledge more accessible and useful.
- Manage and support the AI and Knowledge Management Intern, providing direction, mentorship and quality assurance.

**About You**

You will bring the following experience and skills.

- Demonstrated experience leading or supporting AI adoption, digital transformation, organizational change or technology-enabled improvement initiatives within a complex organization.
- Strong practical understanding of generative AI technologies and their real-world applications, including tools such as Microsoft Copilot and similar AI platforms.

- Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating multiple workstreams across departments and influencing without direct authority.
- Experience leading change-management initiatives and helping teams adopt new tools, processes and ways of working.
- Excellent communication, facilitation and training skills, with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Strong understanding of responsible AI principles, including data protection, confidentiality, cybersecurity, human oversight, transparency, accuracy and ethical considerations.
- Highly organized, pragmatic and collaborative, with the ability to manage competing priorities while building trust and credibility across the organization.
- Experience developing AI strategies, AI adoption programmes, knowledge management approaches or enterprise technology initiatives is highly desirable.
- Experience working within international NGOs, humanitarian organizations or other globally distributed organizations would be an advantage.

fields.title: Senior Conservation Research Assistant (Madagascar)
fields.body:
**Position Overview:**

This is a rare opportunity to live and work in Madagascar, one of the world’s most biodiverse and conservation-critical regions, leading long-term, field-based research in a remote setting. We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Research Assistant (SRA) with a relevant MSc and 1–3 years of practical field research experience to lead SEED Madagascar’s conservation research programme on the ground.

As the Senior Research Assistant, you will oversee the day-to-day operations of SEED’s research camp and play a central role in the design, implementation and reporting of our field-based research. Working closely with SEEDs Conservation Research Programme Coordinator and both international and national staff, you will manage data collection, ensure the quality and integrity of research activities and contribute to the analysis and dissemination of findings to donors and the wider conservation community.

Additionally, you will provide leadership and pastoral support to short-term volunteers, ensuring they receive appropriate training, guidance and supervision during their time in the field. This role is integral to advancing SEED’s mission, combining rigorous scientific research with strong team leadership and collaboration in a challenging but highly rewarding field environment.

*Location:* Fort Dauphin, Madagascar

*Timeframe*: 24 months with potential to extend;

*Terms and conditions:* Local salary to support with accommodation and living costs (field-based food/transport provided); contribution to flights and insurance

**Key Duties and Responsibilities:**

- **Research Leadership**
    - Lead and manage the research team in the field, ensuring effective data collection and high research standards.
    - Lead field-based research on key species and ecosystems, including setting up transects and collecting relevant ecological data.
    - Contribute to the development of new research projects and conservation initiatives, helping to identify priority areas for future work.
    - Support in the expansion of SEED’s research program by fostering relationships with other conservation organisations and researchers.
- **Data Management & Reporting**
    - Ensure data is accurately collected, cleaned and organised in accordance with research protocols.
    - Collaborate with the SCRP Coordinator in data analysis and the preparation of research reports for both internal use and external donors.
    - Contribute to the development of research papers, presentations, and other publications for the international conservation community.
    - Work with the SCRP Coordinator to identify opportunities for research collaborations and funding.
    - Assist in the preparation of proposals and reports for research funding and project development.
- **Volunteer Coordination & Training**
    - Support in the day-to-day management and pastoral care for short-term volunteers, ensuring their well-being and smooth integration into the field team.
    - Lead training sessions for volunteers, ensuring they understand and follow research protocols, data collection methods, and safety procedures.
- **Collaboration & Team Management**
    - Work closely with both the international and national research staff to ensure effective communication and team cohesion.

- **Community Engagement & Outreach**
    - Support the SEED Madagascar team in engaging with communities, including facilitating meetings, conducting surveys, and helping with outreach initiatives.
    - Provide clear interpretation and translation when necessary, ensuring effective communication between international staff and local communities.
- **Logistics & Operations**
    - Assist in managing the logistical aspects of field research, including equipment, transport, and accommodation for staff and volunteers.
    - Oversee the day-to-day operations of the research camp, ensuring smooth logistical coordination and resource management.
- **Policy & Compliance**
    - Ensure compliance with SEED’s policies, including safeguarding, anti-corruption and whistleblowing procedures.
    - Participate in ongoing training to promote adherence to SEED’s health, safety and ethical standards.
- **Additional Tasks**
    - Assist with other tasks as requested by the Director of Programmes and Operations, Conservation Research Coordinator, or Senior Research Assistant within the scope of this role.

**Personal specification:**

- A Masters degree in a conservation-related field
- Proven experience in handling, cleaning, and analysing data, with proficiency in statistical analysis using programming software (e.g., R, Python, or similar)
- At least 1-3 years experience in field data collection, including the use of GPS and/or GIS for mapping and spatial analysis
- Experience in compiling conservation reports, academic papers, or similar documents, with the ability to present data and findings clearly and professionally
- Specialist knowledge of either primatology, herpetology or botany
- Able to or willing to learn to safely handle and identify reptiles and amphibians
- Previous experience of collecting data with a working knowledge of GPS and/or GIS
- Hold a current First Aid certificate
- Demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to SEED Madagascar’s ethos and approach and be a good ambassador for SEED Madagascar at all times
- Have passion, curiosity and motivation for the job and the ability to enthuse others
- Have the ability and desire to work with teams from different economic and cultural backgrounds and across multiple language barriers
- Have the ability and desire to build capacity and share skills across cultures
- Demonstrate proven ability to recognise and appropriately deal with challenging situations
- Demonstrate an awareness of and comfort with increased social and professional responsibility, working at all times with cultural sensitivity and respect
- Demonstrate the ability, social skills and confidence to give clear guidance and support to other members of the team in respect of the philosophy and procedures of SEED Madagascar in order to protect both their safety and the reputation of the NGO
